knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_t\in X\) be the optimization state, \(s_t\in\mathcal S\) the communication or execution state, \(m_t\in\mathcal M\) an encoded message, and \(a_t\in\mathcal A\) a systems action such as client scheduling, precision, topology, synchronization, or transmission power.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative distributed methods whose optimization update and systems decisions are mutually coupled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A communication-system co-design algorithm is a family of measurable policies \((E_t,\Pi_t,D_t,U_t)\) satisfying \[m_t=E_t(x_t,\zeta_t),\qquad a_t=\Pi_t(x_t,s_t,m_t),\qquad \widehat m_t=D_t(m_t,a_t,s_t),\qquad (x_{t+1},s_{t+1})=U_t(x_t,s_t,\widehat m_t,a_t),\] where admissibility imposes declared communication, timing, energy, memory, or synchronization constraints. It is a co-design family when at least one systems action depends on optimization state or accuracy requirements and the resulting communication outcome enters the optimization transition. A design objective may minimize expected terminal error, elapsed time, energy, or a weighted combination subject to resource budgets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication-system co-design jointly specifies message encoding, systems actions, decoding, and optimization-state evolution. A method qualifies when a systems choice such as precision, schedule, topology, or synchronization reacts to optimization information and its communication outcome affects the next optimization state. The admissible policies must state their resource and execution constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled state \((x_t,s_t)\) evolves through both optimization information and admissible systems actions rather than through an optimization recurrence with a fixed communication model.
equivalent_formulations_latex:
The family may be posed as constrained policy optimization \(\min_
\pi\mathbb E[J(x_T,s_T)+\sum_{t<T}c_t(a_t,s_t)]\) over admissible joint policies \(\pi\).
special_cases_latex: Adaptive quantization chooses message precision from the current residual or target accuracy.
Client scheduling chooses participants from both update value and channel state.
Local-step adaptation trades communication frequency against local computation.
immediate_consequences_latex: A fixed compressor within an otherwise unchanged algorithm is a special case but need not exploit bidirectional co-design.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe a particular network, convergence regime, or optimal policy.
Pure hardware implementation choices independent of the optimization state fall outside the stated co-design criterion.

notation.meaning: Systems action selected at round t.

children.title: Compression Operators
children.top_down_role: Lossy communication families used to encode distributed updates.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) carry compressor randomness and let \(Q:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) encode and decode a vector into a communicated representation. Expectations are over this internal randomness conditional on the input.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vector compressors used for distributed states, gradients, residuals, or tracking variables; exact bit encoding is a separate cost specification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compression-operator family is a collection \(\mathcal Q\) of measurable maps \(Q:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) with declared communication cost and an explicit distortion contract. Two canonical contracts are: unbiased bounded variance, \(\mathbb E[Q(x)]=x\) and \(\mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|^2\le\omega\|x\|^2\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R^d\); and contractive compression, \(\mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|^2\le(1-\alpha)\|x\|^2\) for all \(x\), where \(\omega\ge0\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1]\). Membership in the family records which contract and constants hold; neither property is implicit from the word compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compression operator maps a vector to a possibly randomized lossy reconstruction that can be communicated more cheaply under a declared coding model. The operator family is mathematically specified by a distortion condition, commonly unbiased relative variance or mean-square contraction, together with its constants. Unbiased and contractive compressors are distinct families and must not be conflated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each \(Q\in\mathcal Q\) is classified by a stated all-input distortion inequality and, when applicable, the equality \(\mathbb E[Q(x)]=x\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an unbiased compressor, \(\mathbb E\|Q(x)\|^2\le(1+\omega)\|x\|^2\) is equivalent to the variance bound.
A deterministic compressor is represented by a degenerate randomness space.
special_cases_latex: Identity compression has \(\omega=0\) and \(\alpha=1\).
Random sparsification, quantization, and low-rank sketches may satisfy different contracts with method-dependent constants.
immediate_consequences_latex: A contractive compressor may be biased.
An unbiased compressor with large \(\omega\) can introduce substantial update variance.
boundary_notes: The distortion contract does not itself establish a bit count or convergence rate.
Absolute-error compressors require a different inequality and are not covered by the displayed relative contracts.

notation.meaning: Relative mean-square variance parameter for an unbiased compressor.

review_flags: The supplied locator hints were not verified to contain these modern compressor contracts.
A precise compression-operator source locator is required.

children.title: Quantization Methods
children.top_down_role: Reduced-precision encoding of states, gradients, or trackers.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Rounding
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomly selecting an adjacent grid point removes rounding bias while retaining bounded mean-square error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in[k\Delta,(k+1)\Delta]\), output \(k\Delta\) with probability \(((k+1)\Delta-x)/\Delta\) and \((k+1)\Delta\) otherwise. Then \(\mathbb E[Q_\Delta(x)\mid x]=x\) and \(\mathbb E[(Q_\Delta(x)-x)^2\mid x]\le\Delta^2/4\). Coordinatewise application gives \(\mathbb E[\|Q_\Delta(x)-x\|_2^2\mid x]\le d\Delta^2/4\).
assumptions_latex: Each coordinate lies between two finite adjacent grid points.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased scalar quantization between adjacent grid points.

notation.meaning: index of the lower adjacent grid point

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Scalar Quantization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rounding coordinates to a uniform grid gives a deterministic absolute-error bound when no value is clipped.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For spacing \(\Delta>0\), define \(Q_\Delta(x)_j=\Delta\operatorname{round}(x_j/\Delta)\). If no coordinate is clipped, then \(|Q_\Delta(x)_j-x_j|\le\Delta/2\), and therefore \(\|Q_\Delta(x)-x\|_2\le\Delta\sqrt d/2\).
assumptions_latex: Ties use a fixed rounding convention.
No coordinate is saturated or clipped.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise deterministic reduced-precision encoding on an unclipped grid.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Range Saturation Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite reconstruction range produces unbounded absolute error on unbounded inputs unless scaling or overflow handling is added.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a scalar quantizer has reconstruction set \(\mathcal C\subset[-M,M]\), then for every \(|x|>M\), \(|Q(x)-x|\ge |x|-M\). Consequently, no such finite-range quantizer has a finite global input-independent absolute-error bound without a scaling or overflow mechanism.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)\in\mathcal C\subset[-M,M]\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uniform absolute-error guarantees outside a finite reconstruction range.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantization Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-alphabet compression of vectors used in distributed optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be an input domain and let \(\mathcal{C}\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) be a finite codebook. A possibly randomized vector quantizer is a map \(Q:\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{C}\). It is unbiased on \(\mathcal{D}\) when \(\mathbb{E}[Q(x)\mid x]=x\) for every \(x\in\mathcal{D}\). It has relative second-moment parameter \(\omega\ge0\) on \(\mathcal{D}\) when \[\mathbb{E}\!\left[\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\mid x\right]\le\omega\|x\|_2^2\] for every \(x\in\mathcal{D}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-alphabet quantization replaces an input vector by a codebook element; unbiasedness and relative mean-square distortion may be imposed on a specified input domain.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{D}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(\mathcal{C}\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is finite.
The norm is the Euclidean norm on \(\mathbb{R}^d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Using a fixed-length codebook index, \(Q(x)\) can be represented using \(\lceil\log_2|\mathcal{C}|\rceil\) bits, excluding metadata.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-codebook quantizer with unbiasedness and relative variance properties

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be the input domain, \(\mathcal C\) a finite or countable code alphabet, \(E:X\times\Omega\to\mathcal C\) an encoder, and \(D:\mathcal C\to\mathbb R^d\) a decoder.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-precision encoding of distributed vectors; deterministic and randomized scalar or vector quantizers are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quantization method is an encoder--decoder pair whose reconstruction operator is \(Q(x;\xi)=D(E(x;\xi))\) and whose communicated symbol belongs to the declared discrete alphabet \(\mathcal C\). Its specification includes the representable set \(D(\mathcal C)\), code length or alphabet size, treatment of overflow, and a pointwise or stochastic distortion condition. A randomized unbiased quantizer additionally satisfies \(\mathbb E_
\xi[Q(x;\xi)]=x\) for every \(x\in X\); a deterministic uniform scalar quantizer with step \(\Delta>0\) maps each coordinate to a declared grid and, absent clipping, satisfies \(\|Q(x)-x\|_
\infty\le\Delta/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quantization encodes a real vector using a discrete symbol and reconstructs it from a finite- or countable-precision representation. A complete definition states the code alphabet, reconstruction points, bit or symbol cost, overflow behavior, and distortion guarantee. Randomized rounding may preserve the input in expectation, while deterministic uniform rounding provides a coordinatewise absolute-error bound when clipping does not occur.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q=D\circ E\) has discrete communicated output \(E(x;\xi)\in\mathcal C\) and satisfies its declared distortion and, if claimed, unbiasedness conditions for every \(x\in X\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A codebook quantizer can be specified by decision regions \((R_c)_{c\in\mathcal C}\) and reconstruction points \(y_c\), with \(Q(x)=y_c\) for \(x\in R_c\).
special_cases_latex: Coordinatewise uniform quantization uses a regular scalar grid of spacing \(\Delta\).
Stochastic rounding selects adjacent grid points with probabilities chosen so their mean equals the input coordinate.
Sign quantization communicates a scale together with coordinate signs.
immediate_consequences_latex: A finite alphabet on an unbounded input domain requires clipping, adaptive scaling, or unbounded distortion.
Quantization is a compression family distinguished by a discrete reconstruction representation.
boundary_notes: The displayed \(\Delta/2\) bound excludes clipping and assumes nearest-grid rounding.
A countable alphabet does not by itself give a fixed finite bit budget.
review_flags: No supplied source locator was verified to support the exact encoder-decoder and distortion formulation.
A precise quantization source is required before review.

children.title: Sparsification Methods
children.top_down_role: Coordinate selection and sparse update communication.

knowledge_statements.title: Top-k Sparsification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Top-k keeps the largest coordinates, is a best Euclidean k-sparse approximation, and satisfies the sharp uniform contraction bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For x\in\mathbb R^d and 1\le k\le d, let J_k(x) contain indices of k largest values of |x_j|, using a fixed tie rule, and define (T_k(x))_j=x_j\mathbf 1_{\{j\in J_k(x)\}}. Then \|x-T_k(x)\|_2=\min_{\|z\|_0\le k}\|x-z\|_2 and \|x-T_k(x)\|_2^2\le(1-k/d)\|x\|_2^2.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb R^d.
1\le k\le d.
Ties are resolved by a fixed rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic retention of the largest-magnitude coordinates.

notation.meaning: number of nonzero coordinates of z

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsification Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-support compression with sparse transmitted values and indices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparsifier is a possibly randomized map \(S:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d\) such that \(\|S(x)\|_0\le k\) almost surely for every input \(x\), where \(1\le k\le d\). Uniform random-\(k\) sparsification selects a uniformly random subset \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) of size \(k\) and sets \[S(x)_j=\frac{d}{k}x_j\mathbf{1}_{\{j\in I\}}.\] It satisfies \(\mathbb{E}[S(x)\mid x]=x\) and \(\mathbb{E}[\|S(x)-x\|_2^2\mid x]=(d/k-1)\|x\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparsification communicates at most k coordinates; scaled uniform random selection is unbiased with an explicit mean-square distortion.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(1\le k\le d\).
The subset \(I\) is sampled uniformly without replacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transmitted update uses at most \(k\) values and indices while preserving the input in conditional expectation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(d\in\mathbb N\), let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) carry any compressor randomness, and equip \(\mathbb R^d\) with the Euclidean norm. For \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), write \(\operatorname{supp}(x)=\{j:x_j\ne0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic or randomized coordinate sparsification; quantization of retained values and low-rank matrix sketches are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A map \(S:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) is a \(k\)-coordinate sparsifier if, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), there is a measurable index set \(I(x,\xi)\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) with \(|I(x,\xi)|\le k\) almost surely and measurable coefficients \(a_j(x,\xi)\) such that \([S(x,\xi)]_j=a_j(x,\xi)x_j\) for \(j\in I(x,\xi)\) and \([S(x,\xi)]_j=0\) otherwise. Thus \(|\operatorname{supp}(S(x,\xi))|\le k\) almost surely. A sparsification method communicates the selected indices and retained scaled values and reconstructs exactly this sparse vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinate-sparsification compressor on \(\mathbb R^d\) selects at most \(k\) coordinates, possibly as a random or input-dependent function, scales retained entries, and sets every unselected coordinate to zero. Its defining property is the almost-sure support bound \(|\operatorname{supp}(S(x,\xi))|\le k\) for every input \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\text{ is a }k\text{-coordinate sparsifier}\iff \forall x,\ \exists I(x,\xi),\ |I(x,\xi)|\le k\text{ a.s.},\ [S(x,\xi)]_j=a_j(x,\xi)x_j\mathbf 1_{\{j\in I(x,\xi)\}}.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: The support condition is equivalently \(\|S(x,\xi)\|_0\le k\) almost surely for every \(x\), together with coordinatewise retention and scaling.
special_cases_latex: Top-\(k\) sparsification takes \(I(x)\) to be indices of the \(k\) largest values of \(|x_j|\) and uses \(a_j=1\).
Uniform random-\(k\) sparsification samples a size-\(k\) subset and may use \(a_j=d/k\), yielding \(\mathbb E[S(x,\xi)]=x\).
immediate_consequences_latex: At most \(k\) numerical values and their indices need be transmitted per input.
When \(k=d\) and \(a_j=1\), the operator is the identity.
boundary_notes: The support bound alone does not imply unbiasedness, contraction, or an absolute-error guarantee.
Block sparsification requires replacing scalar coordinates by a specified block decomposition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Low-Rank Sketch Compressor for Matrix Updates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(m,n,r\in\mathbb N\) with \(r<\min\{m,n\}\). Matrix updates lie in \(\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), equipped with the Frobenius norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-valued communication represented by rank-constrained factors or sketches; coordinate sparsity is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rank-\(r\) sketch compressor is an encoder-decoder pair \(E:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\times\Omega\to\mathcal Z\) and \(D:\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) whose reconstruction \(C(X,\xi)=D(E(X,\xi))\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(C(X,\xi))\le r\) almost surely for every \(X\). In a factor-sketch realization, the message contains \(U(X,\xi)\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) and \(V(X,\xi)\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and \(C(X,\xi)=U(X,\xi)V(X,\xi)^{\mathsf T}\). A projection-sketch realization may instead communicate products such as \(X\Omega\) and auxiliary information sufficient to reconstruct a rank-at-most-\(r\) approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-rank sketch compressor maps every matrix update \(X\) to a message whose decoded matrix has rank at most \(r\). A canonical factor form transmits matrices \(U\) and \(V\) and reconstructs \(UV^{\mathsf T}\), replacing \(mn\) entries by structured information of order \(r(m+n)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\text{ is rank-}r\text{ sketch compression}\iff C=D\circ E\text{ and }\operatorname{rank}(C(X,\xi))\le r\text{ a.s. for every }X.\)
equivalent_formulations_latex: Every reconstructed matrix admits factors \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) and \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) satisfying \(C(X,\xi)=UV^{\mathsf T}\).
special_cases_latex: Truncated singular-value compression uses \(C(X)=\sum_{j=1}^r\sigma_j u_jv_j^{\mathsf T}\).
For \(r=1\), each reconstruction is an outer product \(uv^{\mathsf T}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A factor message contains \(r(m+n)\) scalars before metadata, compared with \(mn\) scalars for a dense matrix.
If \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\) and the encoder is exact on rank-\(r\) inputs, then \(C(X)=X\).
boundary_notes: A random linear sketch without a specified decoder and rank-constrained reconstruction is not, by this definition, a low-rank compressor.
The rank constraint alone supplies no approximation-error, unbiasedness, or convergence guarantee.
review_flags: No inspected supplied locator supports the exact encoder-decoder and rank-factor formulation.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Sketch Compressor for Matrix Updates
Spectral Error and Exactness of Truncated-Rank Compression
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The spectral error is the first discarded singular value, and truncated-rank compression is lossless exactly when the update rank fits the budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with ordered singular values and rank-\(r\) truncation \(X_r\), \(\|X-X_r\|_2=\sigma_{r+1}(X)\), where \(\sigma_{p+1}(X)=0\) and \(p=\min\{m,n\}\). Consequently, \(X_r=X\) if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\).
assumptions_latex: \(0\le r\le p=\min\{m,n\}\).
Singular values are ordered nonincreasingly.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-norm error and the lossless boundary for truncated-SVD update compression.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Update Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Truncated-SVD compression of a matrix-valued optimization update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\), let \(s=\min\{p,q\}\), and write a thin singular value decomposition \(X=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_s)V^\top\), where \(U\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times s}\), \(V\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times s}\), and \(\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_s\ge0\). For an integer \(r\) with \(0\le r\le s\), define \[X_r=U_{[:,1:r]}\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)V_{[:,1:r]}^\top.\] Then \(X_r\) minimizes \(\|X-Y\|_F\) over matrices \(Y\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\) satisfying \(\operatorname{rank}(Y)\le r\), and \(\|X-X_r\|_F^2=\sum_{j=r+1}^s\sigma_j^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncating a thin singular value decomposition produces a matrix of rank at most r with the best Frobenius-norm reconstruction error among all such matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\), \(p,q\in\mathbb{N}\), and \(r\in\{0,\ldots,\min\{p,q\}\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained singular-vector factors define a rank-at-most-\(r\) message with optimal Frobenius reconstruction error.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Eckart–Young–Mirsky low-rank approximation formula
authoritative_theorem_locator_needed

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Range-Sketch Compression
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random test matrix samples the update's range, and projection onto that range gives a rank-limited reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), draw \(\Omega\in\mathbb R^{n\times\ell}\), form \(Y=X\Omega\), and let \(Q\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\operatorname{range}(Y)\). Reconstruct \(\widehat X=QQ^\top X\), equivalently from transmitted factors \((Q,Q^\top X)\). For every realization, \(\operatorname{rank}(\widehat X)\le\ell\) and \(X-\widehat X=(I-QQ^\top)X\).
assumptions_latex: \(1\le\ell\le\min\{m,n\}\).
The factor-transmission convention is known to encoder and decoder.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided randomized range finding for a matrix-valued update.

notation.meaning: orthonormal basis for the sampled range

knowledge_statements.title: Random Sketch Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear sketch transmission with decoder-based approximate reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\), let \(S\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times s}\) be a random sketching matrix with \(1\le s<q\), and suppose the realization of \(S\) is determined by randomness shared by the encoder and decoder. The encoder transmits \(Y=XS\), and a decoder \(D_S:\mathbb{R}^{p\times s}\to\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\) produces \(\widehat X=D_S(Y)\). Given \(\epsilon\ge0\), \(\delta\in[0,1]\), and a class \(\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\), the pair is an \((\epsilon,\delta)\) Frobenius reconstruction compressor on \(\mathcal{X}\) when \[\Pr_S\!\left(\|D_S(XS)-X\|_F\le\epsilon\|X\|_F\right)\ge1-\delta\] for every \(X\in\mathcal{X}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random linear sketch is transmitted instead of the full matrix, and a decoder reconstructs it with a specified probabilistic relative-error guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(p,q,s\in\mathbb{N}\), \(1\le s<q\), \(\epsilon\ge0\), and \(\delta\in[0,1]\).
The sketch randomness is shared by the encoder and decoder, \(D_S\) is measurable, and the probability is over that randomness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sketch payload contains \(ps\) scalar values; seed, metadata, and scalar-encoding costs are excluded from this count.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: generic encoder-decoder definition for random linear sketch compression
sketch_family_and_reconstruction_model_are_context_dependent
dedicated_source_needed

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Rank–Accuracy Frontier
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discarded singular-value energy decreases with rank, so the first rank meeting the tolerance is cheapest under any monotone rank-cost convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(E_r^2=\sum_{j=r+1}^{p}\sigma_j^2\) and \(r_\varepsilon=\min\{r\in\{0,\ldots,p\}:E_r\le\varepsilon\}\). Then \(E_{r+1}\le E_r\), and \(r_\varepsilon\) is the smallest truncated-SVD rank meeting tolerance \(\varepsilon\). Under any message-cost function nondecreasing in \(r\), it has minimum cost among tolerance-feasible truncated-SVD ranks.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
The declared message cost is nondecreasing in rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_\varepsilon=\min\{r:E_r\le\varepsilon\}\) minimizes the declared monotone cost over tolerance-feasible ranks.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum rank meeting a Frobenius reconstruction tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Budget Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Communication-beneficial ranks for factored matrix-update transmission.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a dense update \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times q}\), direct transmission costs \(pq\) scalar values. Transmitting a rank-\(r\) factorization \(X_r=AB^\top\), with \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times r}\) and \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times r}\), costs \(r(p+q)\) scalar values before metadata and quantization. The factorization reduces this scalar budget exactly when \[r(p+q)<pq,\quad\text{equivalently}\quad r<\frac{pq}{p+q}.\] Under a budget of at most \(B_0\) scalar values, the feasible ranks satisfy \(r\le\lfloor B_0/(p+q)\rfloor\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Low-rank factors save scalar communication only below a dimension-dependent rank threshold; a fixed budget directly limits the feasible rank.
assumptions_latex: \(p,q\in\mathbb{N}\), \(0\le r\le\min\{p,q\}\), and both factors are transmitted densely.
Each transmitted scalar has equal cost, while metadata and numerical precision overhead are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The communication-beneficial regime is \(0\le r<pq/(p+q)\), further restricted by \(r\le\lfloor B_0/(p+q)\rfloor\) when a budget \(B_0\) is imposed.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct parameter counting for dense low-rank factors
bit-level costs require a specified encoding model

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Injectivity Criterion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured class is exactly recoverable precisely when no nonzero difference of two admissible matrices lies in the sketch nullspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(\mathcal S(X)=S\operatorname{vec}(X)\). A decoder satisfying \(D(\mathcal S(X))=X\) for every \(X\in\mathcal X\) exists if and only if \(\ker S\cap\operatorname{vec}(\mathcal X-\mathcal X)=\{0\}\).
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is linear.
The decoder may be defined arbitrarily outside \(\mathcal S(\mathcal X)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Stable-Reconstruction Gain Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Injectivity alone does not ensure stable reconstruction; admissible differences must have uniformly positive sketch gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\alpha_{\mathcal X}=\inf_{X\ne X',\,X,X'\in\mathcal X}\|S\operatorname{vec}(X-X')\|_2/\|X-X'\|_F\). If an \(L\)-Lipschitz decoder on \(\mathcal S(\mathcal X)\) exactly recovers every \(X\in\mathcal X\), then \(\alpha_{\mathcal X}\ge1/L\). Hence \(\alpha_{\mathcal X}=0\) precludes uniformly Lipschitz-stable exact recovery, even if the sketch is injective on \(\mathcal X\).
assumptions_latex: \(D(S\operatorname{vec}(X))=X\) for every \(X\in\mathcal X\).
\(D\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on \(\mathcal S(\mathcal X)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sketch Reconstruction Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and stable recovery of rank-bounded matrices from linear sketches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R^s\) be linear and let \(\mathcal M_r=\{X:\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\}\). Every \(X\in\mathcal M_r\) is uniquely determined by \(\mathcal A(X)\) if and only if \(\ker(\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal M_{2r}=\{0\}\). Define \(\alpha_{2r}=\inf\{\|\mathcal A(H)\|_2:\operatorname{rank}(H)\le2r,\ \|H\|_F=1\}\). Stable reconstruction on \(\mathcal M_r\) requires \(\alpha_{2r}>0\), yielding \(\|X-Y\|_F\le\alpha_{2r}^{-1}\|\mathcal A(X)-\mathcal A(Y)\|_2\). A nonzero rank-at-most-\(2r\) null-space element therefore prevents unique recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sketch recovers every rank-r matrix exactly only when its null space contains no nonzero matrix of rank at most 2r; positive restricted gain gives stability.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n,r,s\in\mathbb N\) with \(r\le\min\{m,n\}\).
\(\mathcal A\) is a linear sketching operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A|_{\mathcal M_r}\text{ is injective}\iff\ker(\mathcal A)\cap\mathcal M_{2r}=\{0\}\).

children.title: Reference-State Predictive Compression Family
children.top_down_role: Encoding innovations relative to stored or predicted states.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_t\in\mathbb R^d\) be a sequence held by a sender. Before round \(t\), sender and receiver possess a synchronized reference \(h_t\in\mathbb R^d\). Let \(Q_t:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) be an innovation compressor.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stateful predictive compression with synchronized encoder-decoder references in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reference-state predictive compressor encodes the innovation \(\delta_t=x_t-h_t\), transmits a representation of \(q_t=Q_t(\delta_t,\xi_t)\), and reconstructs \(\widehat x_t=h_t+q_t\). Its reference update is a shared measurable rule \(h_{t+1}=H_t(h_t,q_t,\widehat x_t)\), evaluated identically by sender and receiver, so their references remain equal whenever initialized equally and supplied the same message. The defining distinction is that the compressed argument is the innovation relative to a reproducible reference, not the full state \(x_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reference-state predictive compression maintains the same reference \(h_t\) at the sender and receiver, compresses only the innovation \(x_t-h_t\), reconstructs \(h_t+Q_t(x_t-h_t)\), and advances both copies of the reference by the same update rule.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The reconstruction error equals the innovation-compression error: \(\widehat x_t-x_t=Q_t(x_t-h_t,\xi_t)-(x_t-h_t)\).
special_cases_latex: With \(h_{t+1}=\widehat x_t\), the decoded state becomes the next prediction reference.
With \(h_t=0\) for all \(t\), the construction reduces to memoryless compression of \(x_t\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Equal initial references and identical received messages imply equal sender and receiver references at every subsequent round.
If \(Q_t(0,\xi)=0\), an input equal to its reference is reconstructed without innovation error.
boundary_notes: Desynchronization caused by packet loss requires an additional recovery or acknowledgment protocol.
No accuracy benefit follows unless the innovations or their compressed errors are controlled.

knowledge_statements.title: Reference-State Predictive Compressor
Variation-Controlled Difference Magnitude
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With the previous state as reference, the encoded value is exactly the state increment, so its magnitude is governed by temporal variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the shared reference is the preceding state, \(h_t=x_{t-1}\), then \(\Delta_t=x_t-x_{t-1}\). Hence \(\|\Delta_t\|=\|x_t-x_{t-1}\|\) and \(\sum_{t=1}^T\|\Delta_t\|=\sum_{t=1}^T\|x_t-x_{t-1}\|\). A bound on one-step state variation is therefore exactly a bound on the compressor input magnitude.
assumptions_latex: Sender and receiver share the exact preceding state as reference.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relation between consecutive-state variation and the encoded innovation.

knowledge_statements.title: Difference Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding an update relative to a shared reference state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a source vector \(x_t\in\mathbb R^d\) and a reference \(s_t\in\mathbb R^d\) known to both endpoints, the encoder forms \(\Delta_t=x_t-s_t\) and transmits \(q_t=Q(\Delta_t)\). The decoder reconstructs \(\widehat x_t=s_t+q_t\). Consequently, \(\widehat x_t-x_t=Q(\Delta_t)-\Delta_t\); thus the reconstruction error is exactly the compression error of the difference rather than that of the full state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transmit a compressed difference from a shared reference and add it back at the decoder; reconstruction error equals the difference-compression error.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t,s_t\in\mathbb R^d\).
\(Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is a possibly randomized compressor.
Encoder and decoder use the same \(s_t\).

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-to-Reconstruction Error Identity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruction error is exactly compression error on the prediction residual, so a smaller residual proportionally reduces distortion under a relative-error compressor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r_t=x_t-h_t, q_t=Q_t(r_t), and \widehat x_t=h_t+q_t. Then \widehat x_t-x_t=Q_t(r_t)-r_t. If \mathbb E[\|Q_t(r)-r\|_2^2\mid r]\le\omega_t\|r\|_2^2 for every r, then \mathbb E[\|\widehat x_t-x_t\|_2^2\mid x_t,h_t]\le\omega_t\|x_t-h_t\|_2^2.
assumptions_latex: x_t,h_t\in\mathbb R^d.
Q_t satisfies the stated conditional relative mean-square error bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Predictive State Compression

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize identical predictor states \(p_0^E=p_0^D\). At round \(t\), the encoder observes \(x_t\), computes \(r_t=x_t-p_t^E\), and sends \(q_t=Q(r_t)\). The decoder outputs \(\widehat x_t=p_t^D+q_t\). Both endpoints then apply the same deterministic transition \(p_{t+1}^E=\Phi(p_t^E,\widehat x_t,q_t)\) and \(p_{t+1}^D=\Phi(p_t^D,\widehat x_t,q_t)\). The procedure stops under the enclosing optimization algorithm's rule and returns the decoded state sequence.

assumptions_latex: \(x_t,p_t^E,p_t^D\in\mathbb R^d\).
\(Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is a compressor.

knowledge_statements.title: Reference-State Synchronization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equal initialization, identical received messages, and identical deterministic updates keep sender and receiver references synchronized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let sender and receiver references be \(h_t^{\mathrm{s}},h_t^{\mathrm{r}}\in\mathbb{R}^d\). Synchronization holds if \(h_0^{\mathrm{s}}=h_0^{\mathrm{r}}\), both endpoints receive the same message \(q_t\), and both update by one deterministic map \(U_t\): \(h_{t+1}^{\mathrm{s}}=U_t(h_t^{\mathrm{s}},q_t)\) and \(h_{t+1}^{\mathrm{r}}=U_t(h_t^{\mathrm{r}},q_t)\). These conditions preserve equality of the references at every round.
assumptions_latex: \(h_0^{\mathrm{s}}=h_0^{\mathrm{r}}\).
Both endpoints apply the same deterministic \(U_t\) to the same \(q_t\).

knowledge_statements.title: Unstable Predictor Amplifies Reference Mismatch
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unstable predictor can geometrically amplify a small initial disagreement between encoder and decoder references.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h_{t+1}^{\mathrm s}=a h_t^{\mathrm s}\) and \(h_{t+1}^{\mathrm r}=a h_t^{\mathrm r}\), with \(|a|>1\) and no resynchronization. If \(h_0^{\mathrm r}-h_0^{\mathrm s}=\delta\ne0\), then \(h_t^{\mathrm r}-h_t^{\mathrm s}=a^t\delta\). Thus an initial reference discrepancy grows geometrically even without additional quantization error.
assumptions_latex: No synchronization correction is applied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar counterexample showing geometric amplification of unsynchronized predictor states.

knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Mismatch Propagation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonexpansive predictor prevents one-step mismatch growth; an expansive Lipschitz bound permits geometric amplification unless synchronization corrects it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If sender and receiver apply the same \(L\)-Lipschitz predictor \(P\), then \(\|P(h_t^{\mathrm r})-P(h_t^{\mathrm s})\|\le L\|h_t^{\mathrm r}-h_t^{\mathrm s}\|\). Therefore \(L\le1\) guarantees nonexpansion in the absence of other errors, whereas an assumption with \(L>1\) permits geometric amplification and supplies no nonexpansion guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
Sender and receiver apply the same predictor.
No synchronization correction or additional mismatch input is applied in this step.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step reference-desynchronization bound for a common predictor map.
review_flags: Corrected the builder's overly strong claim that nonexpansion is possible only when the declared Lipschitz constant is at most one.

knowledge_statements.title: Prediction-Mismatch Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconstruction bias caused by unequal encoder and decoder predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the encoder predicts with \(a_t\), sends \(q_t=Q(x_t-a_t)\), and the decoder predicts with \(b_t\), producing \(\widehat x_t=b_t+q_t\). Then \(\widehat x_t-x_t=(b_t-a_t)+Q(x_t-a_t)-(x_t-a_t)\). Hence prediction mismatch adds directly to compression error. In particular, for the identity compressor \(Q(z)=z\), reconstruction still fails whenever \(a_t\ne b_t\), because \(\widehat x_t-x_t=b_t-a_t\); compressor accuracy alone cannot correct unsynchronized references.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unequal predictions add their mismatch directly to reconstruction error; even lossless residual transmission cannot repair an unsynchronized reference.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t,a_t,b_t\in\mathbb R^d\).
The encoder uses \(a_t\) while the decoder uses \(b_t\).

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) be measurable, and let expectations be conditional on the input \(x\). Fix \(b\ge0\), \(\omega\ge0\), and \(\sigma\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A general finite-dimensional second-moment condition that records bias, relative distortion, and absolute distortion without requiring any one specialized compressor class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The compressor \(C\) satisfies the \((b,\omega,\sigma)\) moment condition if, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), \(\|\mathbb E[C(x,\xi)]-x\|\le b\|x\|\) and \(\mathbb E\|C(x,\xi)-x\|^2\le\omega\|x\|^2+\sigma^2\). The first inequality controls systematic bias; the second permits both input-relative and magnitude-independent reconstruction error. Deterministic compressors are included by treating \(\Omega\) as a singleton. Specialized conditions arise by fixing parameters or replacing these bounds with stronger contraction or pathwise requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compressor satisfies a general moment condition when its mean bias is at most \(b\|x\|\) and its mean-square reconstruction error is at most \(\omega\|x\|^2+\sigma^2\) for every input. The parameters separately expose bias, relative error, and absolute error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x\in\mathbb R^d:\quad \|\mathbb E C(x)-x\|\le b\|x\|,\qquad \mathbb E\|C(x)-x\|^2\le\omega\|x\|^2+\sigma^2.\)
special_cases_latex: Setting \(b=0\) imposes mean preservation when the first bound is attained as equality zero.
Setting \(\sigma=0\) gives a purely relative mean-square error bound; setting \(\omega=0\) gives a uniform absolute mean-square bound.
immediate_consequences_latex: At \(x=0\), the second condition gives \(\mathbb E\|C(0,\xi)\|^2\le\sigma^2\).
If \(\sigma=0\), then \(C(0,\xi)=0\) almost surely.
boundary_notes: These conditions do not specify message length, sparsity, quantization levels, or decoder structure.
Different convergence analyses may require only one inequality or a stronger conditional version relative to an algorithmic filtration.

knowledge_statements.title: Equivalent Output Second-Moment Form
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an unbiased compressor, a relative variance bound is equivalent to an output second-moment bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \mathbb E[Q(x)]=x, then \mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2=\mathbb E\|Q(x)\|_2^2-\|x\|_2^2. Therefore \mathbb E\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le\omega\|x\|_2^2 is equivalent to \mathbb E\|Q(x)\|_2^2\le(1+\omega)\|x\|_2^2. Either form implies Q(0)=0 almost surely.
assumptions_latex: Q(x) has finite second moment for every x.
\mathbb E[Q(x)]=x for every x.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbiased Compressor Conditions

The expectation is over the compressor's internal randomness. Unbiasedness also gives the equivalent second-moment bound \(\mathbb E\|Q(x)\|_2^2\le(1+\omega)\|x\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unbiased compressor preserves every input in expectation and bounds its mean-square compression error proportionally to the input's squared norm.

\(\omega\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Absolute Error Does Not Imply Relative Accuracy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed additive offset has uniformly bounded absolute error but cannot satisfy any global relative-error condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix b\in\mathbb R^d\setminus\{0\} and define Q_b(x)=x+b. Then \|Q_b(x)-x\|_2^2=\|b\|_2^2 for every x, so Q_b has absolute-error parameter \sigma=\|b\|_2. No finite \omega satisfies \|Q_b(x)-x\|_2^2\le\omega\|x\|_2^2 for every x, because the right side vanishes at x=0.

children.title: Deterministic Compressor Conditions
children.top_down_role: Fixed lossy encodings without randomization.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Unbiasedness Is Trivial
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without internal randomness, unbiasedness forces the compressor to be the identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d be deterministic. Expectation over the compressor's internal randomness gives \mathbb E[Q(x)]=Q(x). Hence \mathbb E[Q(x)]=x for every x if and only if Q(x)=x for every x. Thus a nonidentity deterministic lossy compressor cannot be unbiased in this sense.
assumptions_latex: Q has no internal randomness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between deterministic lossy compression and compressor-randomness unbiasedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Compressor Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise distortion conditions for compressors without internal randomness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A deterministic compressor is a fixed map \(Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\): repeated evaluations at the same \(x\) return the same \(Q(x)\), with no expectation over internal randomness. Any claimed distortion guarantee must therefore hold pointwise. For example, relative contractivity with parameter \(\delta\in(0,1]\) means \(\|Q(x)-x\|_2^2\le(1-\delta)\|x\|_2^2\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\). Determinism alone supplies no accuracy bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic compressor is a fixed map, so distortion guarantees are pointwise; absence of randomness by itself does not ensure accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is single-valued and fixed across calls.
For the displayed relative guarantee, \(0<\delta\le1\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(C:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) be a fixed map with no auxiliary random variable, and let \(\rho\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed finite-dimensional lossy encodings governed by a uniform pathwise relative-error condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A deterministic relative-error compressor with factor \(\rho\) is a map \(C:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) satisfying \(\|C(x)-x\|\le\rho\|x\|\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\). Its output is uniquely determined by its input and fixed encoder-decoder state; there is no expectation or probability qualifier. It is deterministically contractive when \(0\le\rho<1\). A communication implementation additionally supplies an encoder \(E\) and decoder \(D\) such that \(C=D\circ E\), but the analytic condition concerns the decoded map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic compressor is a fixed decoded map with no randomization. Under the canonical relative-error condition, every reconstruction differs from its input by at most \(\rho\) times the input norm; it is contractive when \(\rho<1\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The squared form is \(\|C(x)-x\|^2\le\rho^2\|x\|^2\).
special_cases_latex: The identity map has \(\rho=0\).
A fixed Top-\(k\) rule is deterministic once its tie-breaking convention is fixed.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every finite-\(\rho\) deterministic relative-error compressor satisfies \(C(0)=0\).
The triangle inequality gives \(\|C(x)\|\le(1+\rho)\|x\|\).
boundary_notes: Determinism alone does not imply any error bound; the displayed inequality is an additional compressor condition.
Randomized encoders, even with deterministic decoders, are outside this deterministic-map definition.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(u_t\in\mathbb R^d\) be an update to communicate, let \(s_t\in\mathcal S\) be compensation memory, and let \(C_t:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) be a compressor.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General stateful compensation interfaces; residual error feedback, corrected consensus, and compressed gradient tracking are special mechanisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compression-error compensation mechanism is a stateful encoder specified by measurable maps \(A_t:\mathbb R^d\times\mathcal S\to\mathbb R^d\) and \(B_t:\mathbb R^d\times\mathcal S\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathcal S\). At round \(t\), it forms a corrected input \(v_t=A_t(u_t,s_t)\), communicates \(q_t=C_t(v_t,\xi_t)\), and updates memory by \(s_{t+1}=B_t(u_t,s_t,q_t)\). The mechanism is error-compensating when \(s_{t+1}\) explicitly retains information about the untransmitted discrepancy \(v_t-q_t\) and a later corrected input depends on that memory. This distinguishes compensation from independently compressing each \(u_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compression error compensation augments a compressor with memory. It modifies the current update using stored state, compresses that corrected input, and updates the state using the new compression discrepancy so that information omitted now can influence later messages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_t=A_t(u_t,s_t),\qquad q_t=C_t(v_t,\xi_t),\qquad s_{t+1}=B_t(u_t,s_t,q_t),\quad v_{t+1}\text{ depends on retained information from }v_t-q_t.\)
special_cases_latex: Residual error feedback uses \(v_t=u_t+e_t\) and \(e_{t+1}=v_t-q_t\).
Reference-memory compensation may compress \(u_t-h_t\) and update a synchronized reference \(h_t\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(A_t(u,s)=u\) and \(B_t\) discards \(v_t-q_t\), the construction reduces to memoryless compression.
The state dimension and update rule determine which past compression discrepancies can affect future messages.
boundary_notes: The definition supplies a mechanism, not a convergence guarantee.
A state used only for random-number generation is not compensation unless it retains compression-discrepancy information.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncontractive Zero-Compressor Failure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero compressor stores every missing update but never releases it, so the method stagnates and its residual diverges.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Q(v)=0 for every v, e_0=0, and g_t=g\ne0. Then q_t=0 and e_{t+1}=e_t+g=(t+1)g. If the optimizer moves only through q_t, its iterate remains fixed while the residual diverges linearly.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\equiv0\).
The optimizer moves only through transmitted vectors.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual storage cannot compensate for a compressor that never transmits.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Stepsize Weighted Feedback Identity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With varying stepsizes, feedback cancellation includes stepsize-difference terms and is not only a terminal-residual identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Since q_t=g_t+e_t-e_{t+1}, arbitrary finite scalar stepsizes satisfy \[\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\eta_tq_t=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\eta_tg_t+\eta_0e_0+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}(\eta_t-\eta_{t-1})e_t-\eta_{T-1}e_T.\]
assumptions_latex: The scalar stepsizes are finite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary of the usual unweighted cumulative cancellation.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Bound for a Contractive Compressor
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive compressor bounds the feedback residual by a geometric convolution of past update magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For p_t=g_t+e_t, q_t=Q(p_t), and e_{t+1}=p_t-q_t, suppose \|Q(v)-v\|\le\delta\|v\| for all v, with 0\le\delta<1. Then \[\|e_{t+1}\|\le\delta^{t+1}\|e_0\|+\delta\sum_{s=0}^t\delta^{t-s}\|g_s\|.\] If \|g_t\|\le G, then \[\sup_t\|e_t\|\le\|e_0\|+\frac{\delta G}{1-\delta}.\]
assumptions_latex: The standard error-feedback residual recursion is used.
\(\|Q(v)-v\|\le\delta\|v\|\) with \(\delta<1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stability of error-feedback memory under relative compression error.

knowledge_statements.title: Error Feedback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual accumulation and reinjection for compressed optimization updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb R^d\) and residual \(e_0=0\). At round \(t\), obtain an update \(g_t\), form \(u_t=g_t+e_t\), transmit \(q_t=Q(u_t)\), set \(e_{t+1}=u_t-q_t\), and update \(x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_tq_t\). Stop according to the enclosing optimization method and output its designated iterate. The residual recursion gives \(q_t=g_t+e_t-e_{t+1}\), hence \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}q_t=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}g_t+e_0-e_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Error feedback stores each compression residual and adds it to the next update, making cumulative transmitted updates differ only by boundary residuals.
assumptions_latex: \(g_t,e_t,x_t\in\mathbb R^d\).
\(Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is a possibly randomized compressor.
\(\eta_t>0\) is the enclosing method's step size.

knowledge_statements.title: Average-Preservation Boundary for Compensated Consensus
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Error compensation does not itself preserve the network average; the mixing matrix must preserve sums, and row stochasticity alone is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\gamma((W-I_n)\otimes I_d)h^{k+1}\) with \(\gamma\ne0\), the identity \((\mathbf 1^\top\otimes I_d)x^{k+1}=(\mathbf 1^\top\otimes I_d)x^k\) holds for every \(h^{k+1}\) if and only if \(\mathbf 1^\top W=\mathbf 1^\top\). Thus \(W\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1\) alone does not ensure preservation of the arithmetic average.

\(\gamma\ne0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Compensated Consensus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A memory-based compressed consensus step for a fixed mixing matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each agent initialize arbitrary states \(x_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\) and shared reconstruction memories \(h_i^0\in\mathbb R^d\). At iteration \(k\), agent \(i\) sends \(q_i^k=Q(x_i^k-h_i^k)\). Every recipient reconstructs \(\widehat x_i^k=h_i^k+q_i^k\), and the memory is updated by \(h_i^{k+1}=h_i^k+\beta q_i^k\), where \(0<\beta\leq1\). The consensus state update is \[x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k+\gamma\sum_{j=1}^n W_{ij}(\widehat x_j^k-\widehat x_i^k).\] The output after stopping is \((x_1^k,\ldots,x_n^k)\); the accumulated reconstruction memory compensates innovations omitted by compression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents compress deviations from shared memories, update those memories, and mix reconstructed neighbor states; retained reconstruction discrepancies compensate information lost in earlier messages.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonnegative and doubly stochastic.
\(Q:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is a specified compressor.
\(\beta,\gamma\) are chosen so the resulting consensus iteration is stable.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Consensus Budgeting

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose one mixing round contracts disagreement by \(\rho\in(0,1)\): \(\|(I-J)WZ\|\leq\rho\|(I-J)Z\|\). knowledge_statements.title: Consensus-Accuracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three error schedules distinguished by their asymptotic accumulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\varepsilon_k)_{k\geq0}\) bound the consensus error injected at outer iterations. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid Lipschitz sensitivity bound converts the tested message-substitution error into a certified per-event downstream-impact bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the recipient uses \(H_i^k\) satisfying \[\|H_i^k(u)-H_i^k(v)\|\le L_i^k\|u-v\|\] on the relevant region. If transmission is suppressed only when \(\|m_i^k-q_i^k\|\le\tau_i^k\), then \[\|H_i^k(m_i^k)-H_i^k(q_i^k)\|\le L_i^k\tau_i^k.\]
assumptions_latex: The displayed Lipschitz inequality holds on the relevant message region.
Recipients use the same substitute \(q_i^k\) appearing in the test.
The test and sensitivity bound use compatible norms.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a message-substitution threshold into a per-event bound on the omitted update contribution.
review_flags: This is a per-event certificate; accumulation belongs to the Suppression-Error Accumulation sibling.

knowledge_statements.title: Small Local Novelty Can Have Large Downstream Impact
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A message can appear locally redundant yet have arbitrarily large downstream effect when the recipient amplifies small differences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar messages let \(H_c(m)=cm\). Given any novelty threshold \(\tau>0\) and desired impact \(M>0\), choose \(m-q=\tau/2\) and \(c>2M/\tau\). Then \[|m-q|\le\tau\quad\text{but}\quad|H_c(m)-H_c(q)|>M.\] Hence an unscaled message-difference score cannot uniformly control downstream error when sensitivity is unbounded.
assumptions_latex: No uniform upper bound on downstream sensitivity is imposed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calibration failure when message-space novelty is not matched to downstream sensitivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy Score and Suppression Action
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A redundancy rule suppresses a message when a local score is below threshold and uses the explicitly declared cached or predicted substitute.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_i^k\) be a candidate message and \(q_i^k\) the value that recipients can use without receiving it, such as a cached message or a jointly reconstructible prediction. Let \(R_i^k=R(m_i^k,q_i^k,\zeta_i^k)\ge0\) be a locally computable redundancy score. For \(\tau_i^k\ge0\), suppress transmission exactly when \(R_i^k\le\tau_i^k\); on suppression, recipients substitute \(q_i^k\) for \(m_i^k\).
assumptions_latex: The sender can compute the score from locally available information.
Recipients possess or can reconstruct the declared substitute \(q_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_i^k\le\tau_i^k\Longrightarrow m_i^k\text{ is not sent and recipients use }q_i^k.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic local definition tying a redundancy score to the exact substitute used when communication is omitted.

notation.meaning: receiver-available substitute for the omitted message

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Redundancy-Score Variants
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundancy may be measured against a cached message, a shared prediction, or the induced downstream contribution, provided the tested value is the value actually substituted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidate message \(m_i^k\), cached value \(\widehat m_i\), receiver-reconstructible prediction \(\widetilde m_i^k\), and downstream contribution map \(H_i^k\), canonical choices are \[R_{\rm cache}=\|m_i^k-\widehat m_i\|,\qquad R_{\rm pred}=\|m_i^k-\widetilde m_i^k\|,\qquad R_{\rm imp}(q)=\|H_i^k(m_i^k)-H_i^k(q)\|.\] The first authorizes substitution by \(\widehat m_i\), the second by \(\widetilde m_i^k\), and the third directly scores the effect of its declared substitute \(q\). Their thresholds are not interchangeable without comparison bounds.
assumptions_latex: The prediction variant requires sender and receiver to reconstruct the same \(\widetilde m_i^k\).
The impact variant requires the relevant downstream map to be evaluable or soundly bounded.
Each score is paired with the substitute appearing in that score.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_{\rm cache},R_{\rm pred},R_{\rm imp}\text{ control distinct substitution quantities}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Message-novelty, prediction-error, and downstream-impact scores using the actual suppression substitute.

notation.meaning: shared prediction of the current message

knowledge_statements.title: Redundancy-Based Suppression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Suppression determined by the innovation relative to a reconstructible cached message.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_i^k\) be agent \(i\)'s current message and let \(z_i^k\) be a cached message already available to every intended recipient. For a threshold \(\tau_i^k\geq0\), the message is declared redundant and suppressed exactly when \[\lVert m_i^k-z_i^k\rVert\leq\tau_i^k.\] Recipients then use \(z_i^k\), producing a substitution error \(r_i^k=m_i^k-z_i^k\) satisfying \(\lVert r_i^k\rVert\leq\tau_i^k\). If the inequality fails, the current message is transmitted and becomes the new common cache.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A message is suppressed when it is close enough to a recipient-reconstructible cache, with the suppression threshold directly bounding the substitution error.
assumptions_latex: \(m_i^k,z_i^k\) lie in a common normed vector space.
\(z_i^k\) is available to every intended recipient.
\(\tau_i^k\geq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Skipped-Innovation Accumulation Bound
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stale-message error is the sum of innovations since the last transmission, so bounded refresh age or bounded skipped-interval variation controls accumulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(t(k)\le k\) be the last transmission time and \(\hat m^k=m^{t(k)}\). Then \[m^k-\hat m^k=\sum_{j=t(k)+1}^{k}(m^j-m^{j-1}),\qquad \|m^k-\hat m^k\|\le\sum_{j=t(k)+1}^{k}\|m^j-m^{j-1}\|.\] If \(k-t(k)\le H\) and every one-step innovation is at most \(\delta\), then \(\|m^k-\hat m^k\|\le H\delta\).
assumptions_latex: \(m^k\) lies in a normed vector space.
\(\hat m^k=m^{t(k)}\), where \(t(k)\) is the last transmission time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|m^k-\hat m^k\|\le\sum_{j=t(k)+1}^{k}\|m^j-m^{j-1}\|\); bounded age and increments imply \(\|m^k-\hat m^k\|\le H\delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact accounting of staleness accumulated since the last transmitted message.

knowledge_statements.title: Suppression-Error Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic perturbation boundary for communication-suppressed distributed iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the communicated state satisfy \(x^{k+1}=T_k(x^k)+e^k\), and let the unsuppressed reference satisfy \(y^{k+1}=T_k(y^k)\) with \(x^0=y^0\). If every \(T_k\) is nonexpansive, then \(\|x^K-y^K\|\leq\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|e^k\|\). Thus summable suppression errors give uniformly bounded accumulated deviation. Without cancellation or contraction, a persistent error need not vanish: for \(T_k(z)=z\) and \(e^k=e\neq0\), one has \(x^K-y^K=Ke\), so suppression error grows linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonexpansive iterations accumulate suppression errors by at most their norm sum; a constant uncancelled error can instead produce deviation growing linearly with the number of rounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x^K-y^K\|\leq\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|e^k\|\), while constant nonzero errors can yield \(\|x^K-y^K\|=K\|e\|\).

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Communication Accuracy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method converts a progress-dependent accuracy target into the minimum geometric-mixing budget needed at each optimization iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), select a target communication error \(\varepsilon_k>0\) from locally or globally available progress information. Given a disagreement bound \(D_k\) and mixing contraction \(\rho\in(0,1)\), choose \(s_k=\max\{0,\lceil\log(D_k/\varepsilon_k)/\log(1/\rho)\rceil\}\), interpreting the logarithmic term as zero when \(D_k\leq\varepsilon_k\). Apply \(s_k\) consensus rounds, producing \(\widetilde Z^k=W^{s_k}Z^k\), and then execute the prescribed optimization update. Stop under the outer criterion and report both the terminal iterate and cumulative communication \(\sum_{t< K}s_t\).
assumptions_latex: One mixing round contracts disagreement by a known \(\rho\in(0,1)\).
A valid bound \(D_k\) on current disagreement is available.
The target sequence \((\varepsilon_k)\) is generated by a prescribed adaptation rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected budget guarantees \(\|(I-J)\widetilde Z^k\|\leq\varepsilon_k\) whenever \(\|(I-J)Z^k\|\leq D_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Communication effort increases or decreases according to an outer-iteration accuracy target.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let agents communicate vectors in \(\mathbb R^d\) at optimization iterations \(k\in\mathbb N\). Let \(Q_k:\mathbb R^d\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^d\) be the possibly randomized encoder-decoder map used at iteration \(k\), and let \(\mathcal F_k\) contain the history before that communication.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional distributed optimization with iteration-dependent lossy communication; the definition covers deterministic or conditionally randomized errors but does not assert convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An adaptive communication-accuracy schedule is a sequence \((Q_k,\varepsilon_k)_{k\ge0}\) with \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\), where \(Q_k\) may be selected using \(\mathcal F_k\), such that every transmitted \(v_k\in\mathbb R^d\) satisfies a prescribed conditional error criterion, for example \(\mathbb E[\|Q_k(v_k)-v_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le \varepsilon_k^2\). The schedule is vanishing if \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), summably accurate if \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\), and relatively accurate if there are \(\omega_k\ge0\) such that \(\mathbb E[\|Q_k(v)-v\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\omega_k\|v\|^2\) for all admissible \(v\). Adaptivity means that the accuracy parameter or coding rule is chosen from the available history rather than fixed uniformly over all iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive communication accuracy is an iteration-indexed, history-measurable choice of coding rule and error tolerance. Every communicated vector must obey the stated conditional error bound. Accuracy is vanishing when the absolute tolerances tend to zero, summably accurate when they are summable, and relatively accurate when error is bounded by an iteration-dependent multiple of the input norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\|Q_k(v_k)-v_k\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\varepsilon_k^2\), with \((Q_k,\varepsilon_k)\) selectable from \(\mathcal F_k\).

special_cases_latex: A fixed-accuracy compressor has \(Q_k=Q\) and \(\varepsilon_k=\varepsilon\) for every \(k\).
A progressively refined quantizer is represented by \(\varepsilon_{k+1}\le\varepsilon_k\) and \(\varepsilon_k\to0\).

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be the agents. A global event counter \(k\in\mathbb N\) is used only for analysis. Let \(A(k)\subseteq V\) be the agents updating at event \(k\), and let \(\tau_{ij}(k)\le k\) be the timestamp of agent \(j\)'s value used by agent \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract execution semantics for computation and message use, independent of a particular optimization update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A synchronization model is a class \(\mathfrak S\) of admissible schedules \(s=((A(k)),(\tau_{ij}(k)))_{k\ge0}\) satisfying declared timing, activation, and information-age constraints. Synchronous execution imposes \(A(k)=V\) and \(\tau_{ij}(k)=k\) at every round. Bounded-delay asynchrony permits irregular activations but requires a finite \(B\) such that \(0\le k-\tau_{ij}(k)\le B\) whenever a stored value is used, together with a declared fairness condition. Total asynchrony removes a uniform finite delay bound but requires every agent to update infinitely often and timestamps used along an infinite update sequence to tend to infinity. Partial barriers impose progress after a declared subset, quorum, or deadline condition is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronization model is a set of admissible activation and message-timestamp schedules. It states which agents update, how old each value may be, and what fairness or barrier rules apply. Synchronous, bounded-delay asynchronous, totally asynchronous, and partial-barrier models are distinguished by different constraints on these schedules, not by the optimization formula itself.

special_cases_latex: Lockstep rounds correspond to \(A(k)=V\) and zero information age.
Serial coordinate execution corresponds to \(|A(k)|=1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Execution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All required workers use the same round state, and the next state is committed only after the full barrier completes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For workers \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), synchronous execution consists of rounds \(k=0,1,\ldots\). At the start of round \(k\), every worker receives the same committed state \(x^k\), computes \(u_i^k\), and returns it before the next state is committed. The coordinator waits for every required worker and applies \[x^{k+1}=\Phi_k\!\left(x^k,u_1^k,\ldots,u_m^k\right).\] No worker begins computation for round \(k+1\) using an uncommitted state, and no update tagged with a different round enters this aggregation.
assumptions_latex: The required worker set \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is fixed for each round.
Each returned update carries its round index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle x^{k+1}=\Phi_k(x^k,u_1^k,\ldots,u_m^k)\) uses only updates computed from \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round-based execution with a full coordination barrier.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lockstep, barrier-separated execution with coordinated rounds; computation times may differ physically, but logical progress waits for the round condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An execution is synchronous if there is a sequence of global rounds \(k=0,1,\ldots\) such that every participating agent computes round-\(k\) messages from round-\(k\) states, every message admitted to the round-\(k\) update is labeled \(k\), and no agent begins its logical round-\(k+1\) update before the prescribed round-\(k\) barrier is satisfied. In the full-participation, reliable-message model, \(A(k)=V\) and the update has the form \(x_i^{k+1}=\Phi_i^k(x_i^k,(m_{ji}^k)_{j\in N_i})\). Thus the information timestamp used at round \(k\) is \(\tau_{ij}(k)=k\), unless a separately specified delayed synchronous model is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronous execution consists of globally indexed rounds separated by barriers. All participating agents form round-k messages from round-k states, and admitted messages have that round's label. No agent logically advances to the next round until the specified barrier is met. In the full-participation model every agent updates once per round using current-round neighbor information.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Logical synchrony is equivalently a barrier ordering in which all required round-\(k\) operations precede every round-\(k+1\) state update.
special_cases_latex: A centralized parameter-server round is synchronous when the server waits for all prescribed worker messages before broadcasting the next state.
immediate_consequences_latex: No iterate mixes messages bearing different logical round indices in the full lockstep model.

Waiting for only a quorum is partial-barrier rather than full synchronous execution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round-indexed execution that bounds waiting but does not require all agents at every barrier; treatment of late messages must be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partial-barrier deadline regime releases round \(k\) at stopping time \(T_k=\inf\{t\ge0:|R_k(t)|\ge q_k\}\wedge D_k\). The participating set is \(A(k)=R_k(T_k)\), and the next logical state is computed using only the messages admitted by a declared late-message policy. The regime is a strict partial barrier when \(q_k<n\) is permitted. A valid specification states whether messages arriving after \(T_k\) are discarded, carried into a later round with timestamps, or used by an asynchronous correction; without that rule, the execution semantics are incomplete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial-barrier deadline execution advances when either a required quorum of responses has arrived or a deadline expires. The agents whose responses are admitted form that round's participating set. Because the quorum may be smaller than the full network, progress need not wait for every agent. The model must state how late messages are treated.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A fixed-fraction barrier uses \(q_k=\lceil\alpha n\rceil\) for some \(\alpha\in(0,1]\).
special_cases_latex: If \(q_k=n\) and \(D_k=+\infty\), the rule reduces to a full barrier.
If the quorum is never reached before \(D_k\), release occurs exactly at the deadline.
immediate_consequences_latex: The waiting time satisfies \(T_k\le D_k\).
The number of admitted responses can be smaller than \(q_k\) when the deadline fires first.

Semi-Synchronous Execution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers may advance in unequal cohorts, but the difference between the fastest and slowest progress counters remains uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_i(t)\in\mathbb{N}\) denote the number of updates completed by worker \(i\) by time \(t\). Execution is semi-synchronous with skew bound \(\Delta\in\mathbb{N}\) if workers may progress without a full barrier but the scheduler enforces \[\max_i s_i(t)-\min_i s_i(t)\le\Delta\quad\text{for every }t.\] Aggregations may use proper subsets of workers, but a worker whose progress would violate the bound is paused until lagging workers advance. The case \(\Delta=0\) reduces to lockstep progress; positive \(\Delta\) permits controlled overlap between computation rounds.

Each completed update increments exactly one progress counter.
\(\Delta\) is a fixed nonnegative integer.

knowledge_statements.title: Deadline-Induced Selection Bias
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If timely responses correlate with worker identity or data, averaging only on-time gradients can be biased even when the full gradient is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two equally weighted workers with deterministic local gradients \(g_1=1\) and \(g_2=-1\), so the full gradient is \((g_1+g_2)/2=0\). Suppose worker \(1\) always responds before a deadline and worker \(2\) never does. A deadline aggregator averaging available gradients therefore returns \[\widehat g=\frac{1}{|A|}\sum_{i\in A}g_i=g_1=1,\] not the full gradient. More generally, if response inclusion depends on worker identity, data, or gradient magnitude, then conditioning on timely response changes the sampling distribution and need not preserve unbiasedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise Bounded-Staleness Read Model
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded delay can constrain each component's age while allowing an inconsistent snapshot assembled from several recent versions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let x^0,x^1,\ldots denote committed shared states. knowledge_statements.title: Conservative Buffered Tracker Transport
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conservative splitting, buffering, delivery, and gradient-difference injection preserve total tracker mass despite delayed messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain held tracker masses \(y_i\), directed-channel buffers \(b_{ij}\), and gradients \(g_i=\nabla f_i(x_i)\). A send event at \(i\) chooses nonnegative fractions \(a_{ji}\) summing to one, replaces \(y_i\) by \(a_{ii}y_i^{\rm old}\), and adds \(a_{ji}y_i^{\rm old}\) to each outgoing buffer \(b_{ij}\). A receive event transfers one buffer to its receiver and zeros that buffer. When \(x_i\) changes, inject \(g_i^+-g_i^-\) into \(y_i\). Then \[\mathcal M=\sum_i y_i+\sum_{(i,j)}b_{ij}\] changes only by the injected gradient difference and equals \(\sum_i g_i\) at every event when initialized that way.
assumptions_latex: Every undelivered message is represented by a channel buffer.
Send fractions are nonnegative and sum to one, including retained mass.
Each delivered buffer is transferred exactly once.
Initially \(\mathcal M=\sum_i g_i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The defect between total augmented tracker mass and the current aggregate gradient exactly tests the tracking invariant when in-transit mass is included.

The test is sound only when all held and in-transit tracker mass is included in \(Y^k\).

Then \[y_1^{k+1}+y_2^{k+1}=\tfrac12(a+3b)\ne a+b\] whenever \(a\ne b\), although \(W\) is doubly stochastic.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite communication graph and \((\mathcal F_k)\) the execution filtration. At event \(k\), let \(A_k\subseteq V\), \(H_k\subseteq E\), and \(B_k\subseteq\{1,cldots,d\}\) denote active nodes, edges, and coordinate blocks.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A randomized network-activation model is a stochastic process \((A_k,H_k,B_k)_{k\ge0}\) adapted after sampling to \((\mathcal F_{k+1})\), with conditional law \(P_k(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_k)\). It is node activation when the primitive random unit is \(A_k\); edge activation when it is \(H_k\); block activation when computation or communication is restricted to \(B_k\); and joint activation when two or more units are sampled together. The model is conditionally independent when \(P_k\) does not depend on earlier activations beyond declared exogenous state, Markovian when it depends on a current activation state, and history-dependent otherwise. Persistent excitation requires a stated positivity condition, such as \(\mathbb P(i\in A_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p_i>0\) almost surely for every required node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized activation model specifies conditional distributions for active nodes, edges, and coordinate blocks at each event. knowledge_statements.title: Activation-Coverage Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coverage may require every component within each bounded window, positive conditional window probability, or merely infinitely many activations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

\[
\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B-1}A_t=\mathcal C\quad\text{for every }k;
\]

\[
\mathbb{P}\!\left(c\in\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B-1}A_t\mid\mathcal F_k\right)\ge\eta
\]
for every \(c\in\mathcal C\) and \(k\); and eventual coverage, when every \(c\) belongs to \(A_k\) for infinitely many \(k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Distributed ADMM
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers solve local ADMM subproblems using possibly delayed consensus values. A coordinator aggregates available states, while only activated workers update their dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x_1,\ldots,x_m,z}\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) subject to \(x_i=z\), initialize \(x_i^0,z^0,u_i^0\) and choose \(\rho>0\). At event \(k\), activate a nonempty worker set \(S_k\). Each \(i\in S_k\) reads a delayed master value \(z^{\tau_i(k)}\) and computes \[x_i^{k+1}\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{x_i}\left\{f_i(x_i)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert x_i-z^{\tau_i(k)}+u_i^k\rVert^2\right\};\] inactive workers retain their values. After receiving the selected updates, the coordinator sets \(z^{k+1}=m^{-1}\sum_i(x_i^{k+1}+u_i^k)\), and each activated worker sets \(u_i^{k+1}=u_i^k+x_i^{k+1}-z^{k+1}\); inactive dual variables are retained. Stop when primal and dual residual tolerances hold.
assumptions_latex: Every worker is activated infinitely often and \(0\le k-\tau_i(k)\le D<\infty\).
Each \(f_i\) is proper, closed, and convex, and a primal-dual solution exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs the latest \((x_1^k,\ldots,x_m^k,z^k,u_1^k,\ldots,u_m^k)\) when its prescribed residual test is met.

Choosing \(\pi=\mathbf1/m\) imposes preservation of the arithmetic mean.

Semidefinite Representation of Fastest Mixing
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fastest symmetric mixing-weight design is an SDP that bounds the disagreement operator between two semidefinite inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\) and let \(\mathcal W_G\) be the symmetric, nonnegative, row-stochastic matrices supported on an undirected graph \(G\). Then \[\min_{W\in\mathcal W_G}\|W-J\|_2=\min_{W,t}\{t:-tI\preceq W-J\preceq tI,\ W\in\mathcal W_G\}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a fixed finite undirected graph.
Self-weights are permitted.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex epigraph formulation of symmetric mixing-weight design on a fixed topology.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixing-Weight Design
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose graph-compatible symmetric stochastic weights minimizing disagreement contraction, then apply the resulting matrix until successive consensus iterates differ by at most the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a connected undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) with \(|V|=n\), set \(J=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}/n\) and compute \[W^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{W}\ \lVert W-J\rVert_2\] subject to \(W=W^{\mathsf T}\), \(W\mathbf 1=\mathbf 1\), \(W_{ij}\geq0\), and \(W_{ij}=0\) whenever \(i\neq j\) and \(\{i,j\}\notin E\). Initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^n\), iterate \(x^{k+1}=W^\star x^k\), and stop when \(\lVert x^{k+1}-x^k\rVert_2\leq\varepsilon\). The design minimizes the worst contraction factor on \(\mathbf 1^\perp\) among feasible symmetric weights.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite, undirected, and connected.
Self-weights \(W_{ii}\) are permitted.
\(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{W}\lVert W-J\rVert_2\) over the stated feasible set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fastest-consensus weight design for a fixed undirected communication graph.
