knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Cost Connected Topology
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With connectivity as the only requirement, a minimum spanning tree is an exact least-cost topology.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \((V,E_0)\) is an undirected candidate graph with nonnegative additive link costs and connectivity is the sole requirement, any minimum spanning tree is an optimal topology. A feasible connected topology exists exactly when \((V,E_0)\) is connected.
assumptions_latex: Candidate links are undirected.
Link costs are nonnegative and additive.
No degree, diameter, reliability, or spectral constraint is imposed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connectivity-only specialization for static undirected topology design.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Spanning-Tree Fundamental-Cut Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tree is minimum-cost exactly when every tree edge is cheapest across its fundamental cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A spanning tree \(T\) is minimum-cost if and only if, for every \(e\in T\), edge \(e\) has minimum cost among candidate edges crossing the cut induced by deleting \(e\), with ties allowed.
assumptions_latex: The finite candidate graph is connected and undirected.
Edge costs are additive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{ is an MST}\iff c_e=\min\{c_f:f\in\delta(S_e)\}\quad\forall e\in T.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate for connectivity-only undirected topology design.

notation.meaning: one component after deleting tree edge e

knowledge_statements.title: Topology-Constraint Complexity Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Connectivity-only topology design is tractable, while common structural or performance-constrained variants can be NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimum-cost undirected connectivity is polynomial-time solvable by a minimum spanning tree. Standard variants with additional degree, diameter, survivability, or spectral-performance requirements include NP-hard problems, so a complexity claim must name its constraint family.
assumptions_latex: Inputs are finitely and rationally encoded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Connectivity-only design is in \(\mathbf P\); standard constrained topology-design families include NP-hard cases.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between connectivity-only and constrained topology design.
review_flags: The NP-hardness claim is existential across named constrained families, not universal for every additional constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Static Communication-Topology Design
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static topology design selects communication links under declared cost, feasibility, and graph-performance requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finite nodes \(V\), candidate links \(E_0\), admissible family \(\mathcal G\subseteq2^{E_0}\), cost \(C(E)\), and topology performance measure \(\Phi(E)\), static topology design selects \[E^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{E\in\mathcal G}C(E)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\Phi(E)\le q.\] Mixing weights are not decision variables in this topology-only formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and \(E_0\) are finite.
The admissible family and performance measure are explicitly declared.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topology-only selection with fixed candidate links, costs, and graph-performance constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Survivable Topology Design
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-edge-survivable topology places at least k selected links across every proper cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integer \(k\ge2\), solve \(\min_{E\subseteq E_0}\sum_{e\in E}c_e\) subject to \(|E\cap\delta(S)|\ge k\) for every nonempty proper \(S\subset V\). These constraints are equivalent to connectivity after deletion of any \(k-1\) selected edges.
assumptions_latex: Candidate links are undirected.
Failures are arbitrary edge deletions.
Costs are additive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static redundancy-constrained undirected graph selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Cost Rooted Directed Topology
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rooted directed reachability is optimized by a minimum-cost out-arborescence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A minimum-cost spanning out-arborescence rooted at \(r\) is the least-cost selected topology containing a directed path from \(r\) to every vertex. It exists exactly when every vertex is reachable from \(r\) and is computable by the Chu–Liu–Edmonds algorithm.
assumptions_latex: The candidate graph is finite and directed.
Arc costs are additive.
Only rooted outward reachability is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A^\star\in\arg\min\left\{\sum_{a\in A}c_a:A\text{ is a spanning out-arborescence rooted at }r\right\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed rooted-reachability specialization.

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-Topology Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budget-constrained undirected topology selection through algebraic-connectivity maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(E_c\) be candidate undirected links with costs \(c_e>0\), incidence vectors \(b_e\), and budget \(B\). A topology maximizing algebraic connectivity solves
\[\max_{z,t}\ t\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{e\in E_c}z_e b_e b_e^\top\succeq t\left(I-\frac{\mathbf1\mathbf1^\top}{n}\right),\quad \sum_{e\in E_c}c_ez_e\le B,\quad z_e\in\{0,1\}.\]
The selected graph contains exactly the links with \(z_e=1\). Its optimal \(t\) equals the largest achievable Laplacian eigenvalue \(\lambda_2\); positive \(t\) certifies connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication links can be selected under a cost budget by maximizing the second Laplacian eigenvalue; a positive optimum certifies a connected chosen topology.
assumptions_latex: \(E_c\) is a finite candidate edge set on \(n\) vertices.
Each link has positive cost and the budget is \(B\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model maximizes \(\lambda_2\) of the selected graph Laplacian, and \(t>0\) implies connectivity.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a spanning tree of a weighted undirected candidate graph. If for every tree edge \(e\in T\), removing \(e\) induces a cut \((S,V\setminus S)\) for which \(e\) has minimum weight among all candidate edges crossing that cut, then \(T\) is a minimum spanning tree. Conversely, every minimum spanning tree satisfies this condition with ties allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spanning tree is minimum-cost exactly when each tree edge is a cheapest edge across its fundamental cut, allowing ties.
assumptions_latex: The candidate graph is finite, connected, and undirected.
Edge costs are real and additive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{ is an MST}\iff c_e=\min\{c_f:f\in\delta(S_e)\}\quad\forall e\in T.

Alternating Topology–Weight Co-Design
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating exact topology and weight updates decrease a common objective, without a generic global-optimality guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a joint objective \(F(E,W)\), compute \[W^{r+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{W:(E^r,W)\text{ feasible}}F(E^r,W),\qquad E^{r+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{E:(E,W^{r+1})\text{ feasible}}F(E,W^{r+1}).\] Exact block minimization gives \(F(E^{r+1},W^{r+1})\le F(E^r,W^r)\), but does not by itself imply convergence to a global optimum.
assumptions_latex: Both block subproblems attain minimizers.
Both steps use the same declared objective.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-coordinate procedure for a declared static joint objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Information Online Graph–Weight Adaptation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exponential weighting adapts graph-weight choices to observed communication and mixing losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\) be a finite family of implementable graph-weight pairs and \(\ell_k(d)\in[0,1]\). Initialize \(q_1(d)=1\), sample \(d_k\) with probability \(q_k(d)/\sum_{d'}q_k(d')\), observe all losses, and set \(q_{k+1}(d)=q_k(d)e^{-\eta\ell_k(d)}\). Use the matrix in \(d_k\) for round \(k\).
assumptions_latex: The feasible design family is finite and nonempty.
Every pair is graph-compatible and implementable.
Full-information losses lie in \([0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observation-driven selection from a finite feasible family.
review_flags: Bandit feedback requires a different estimator and bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Family Online Search Cost
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Naive online co-adaptation scales linearly with the number of feasible designs per round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintaining explicit weights for \(M\) graph-weight pairs uses \(O(M)\) storage and \(O(M)\) arithmetic per full-information round, excluding loss evaluation.
assumptions_latex: All design weights and updates are explicit.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit implementation cost of exponential weighting.

knowledge_statements.title: Per-Round Connectivity Is Not Necessary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disconnected instantaneous graphs can still produce consensus through bounded-window joint connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On three nodes, alternate \(E_{2r}=\{\{1,2\}\}\) and \(E_{2r+1}=\{\{2,3\}\}\), using positive self-weights and pairwise averaging on the active edge. Every instantaneous graph is disconnected, but every two-round union is connected and repeated products contract disagreement.
assumptions_latex: Active-edge averaging uses positive self- and edge weights.
The two-edge pattern repeats.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_k\) disconnected for every \(k\) does not imply failure of consensus.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary preventing overstrong feasibility requirements for time-varying co-adaptation.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Weight–Topology Adaptation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint adaptation changes links and graph-compatible weights together, with each decision influencing the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A joint adaptation is a sequence \((E_k,W_k)\) with \(E_k\subseteq E_0\), where each \(W_k\) satisfies the declared stochasticity conditions and \((W_k)_{ij}=0\) for every off-diagonal pair \(\{i,j\}\notin E_k\). It is genuinely joint when topology choice depends on attainable weighted-mixing performance or weight choice depends on topology costs.
assumptions_latex: The node and candidate-link sets are fixed.
Every selected matrix is implementable on its selected graph.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled time-varying choice of active edges and compatible mixing weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Product-Contraction Criterion
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adapted graph-weight sequence reaches average consensus exactly when its matrix products contract disagreement; uniform block contraction gives a geometric bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/n\) and let every nonnegative \(W_k\) be doubly stochastic. For \(x^{k+1}=W_kx^k\), average consensus for every initial state is equivalent to \[\|(W_{k-1}-J)\cdots(W_0-J)\|_2\to0.\] If for some \(B\ge1\) and \(\rho<1\), every length-\(B\) block product has norm at most \(\rho\), then disagreement contracts geometrically by block.
assumptions_latex: Every \(W_k\) is nonnegative and doubly stochastic.
All matrices act on the same finite node set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence interface for an adapted sequence of mixing operators.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the consensus subspace

knowledge_statements.title: Regret and Consensus under Uniformly Contractive Online Choices
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-family adaptation has sublinear full-information regret, while uniform contraction guarantees geometric consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M=|\mathcal D|\), exponential weighting satisfies \(\mathbb E\sum_{k=1}^K\ell_k(d_k)-\min_d\sum_{k=1}^K\ell_k(d)\le\log(M)/\eta+\eta K/8\). With \(\eta=\sqrt{8\log(M)/K}\), regret is at most \(\sqrt{K\log(M)/2}\). If every selectable \(W\) is doubly stochastic and \(\|W-J\|_2\le\rho<1\), then \(\|x^K-Jx^0\|_2\le\rho^K\|x^0-Jx^0\|_2\).
assumptions_latex: Losses lie in \([0,1]\).
For consensus, every feasible matrix is doubly stochastic and uniformly contractive.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint guarantee for finite full-information adaptation.
review_flags: Uniform per-round contraction is sufficient but stronger than bounded-window joint connectivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Cut Impossibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If communication permanently stops across a cut, no compatible local averaging scheme can guarantee global consensus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a nonempty proper set \(S\subset V\) and \(k_0\) exist such that no \(G^k\), \(k\ge k_0\), contains an edge crossing \((S,V\setminus S)\). Every compatible mixing product after \(k_0\) is block diagonal across that cut, so initial states having different constants on the two sides cannot reach global consensus.
assumptions_latex: Mixing is graph-compatible.
A proper cut has no crossing edge after a finite time.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-flow obstruction for switching undirected topologies.

notation.meaning: one side of the persistent communication cut

knowledge_statements.title: Topology-Feasibility Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed undirected topology supports strict average-consensus contraction exactly when it is connected; disconnection leaves an invariant nonconsensus direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph and permit nonnegative self-weights. There exists a symmetric matrix \(W\) satisfying \(W\mathbf1=\mathbf1\), \(W_{ij}=0\) for every absent off-diagonal edge, and \(\lVert W-J\rVert_2<1\), with \(J=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/|V|\), if and only if \(G\) is connected. If \(G\) is disconnected, every compatible stochastic \(W\) has a nonconsensus vector \(v\perp\mathbf1\) with \(Wv=v\), so strict contraction of all disagreement vectors is impossible.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and undirected.
Mixing weights are symmetric and nonnegative.
Self-weights are permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists W:\lVert W-J\rVert_2<1\) if and only if \(G\) is connected.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp connectivity boundary for symmetric average-consensus mixing.

children.top_down_role: Temporal allocation of links, nodes, and communication rounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Periodic and Randomized Feasible Scheduling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Periodic schedules provide deterministic recurrence bounds; positive-probability randomized schedules provide almost-sure recurrence without deterministic bounded gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty \(\mathcal F\subseteq2^{\mathcal A}\), a periodic policy selects \(S_0,\ldots,S_{P-1}\in\mathcal F\) and sets \(S_k=S_{k\bmod P}\). An i.i.d. randomized policy draws \(S_k\sim p\) on \(\mathcal F\). A resource appearing in a period has activation gap at most \(P\). Under the randomized policy, \(\Pr(a\in S_k)>0\) implies activation infinitely often almost surely, but generally gives no deterministic gap bound.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) and \(P\) are finite.
Randomized rounds are independent and identically distributed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical open-loop policies over a declared feasible family.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximum-Weight Feasible Activation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activate a feasible set of communication resources having maximum total current priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given nonnegative priorities \(w_a^k\) and a finite nonempty feasible family \(\mathcal F_k\), select \[S_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{S\in\mathcal F_k}\sum_{a\in S}w_a^k.\] Under node-exclusive link interference, feasible sets are matchings; on a bipartite communication graph the subproblem is maximum-weight bipartite matching.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F_k\) is finite and nonempty.
Priorities are known before round \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interference-aware priority scheduling for one communication round.

knowledge_statements.title: Bipartite Matching-Schedule Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible matching and equal-valued feasible vertex potentials certify maximum-weight scheduling optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a bipartite graph with edge weights \(w_{ij}\), a matching \(M\) is maximum weight if there are potentials \(u_i,v_j\ge0\) satisfying \(u_i+v_j\ge w_{ij}\) for every edge and \[\sum_i u_i+\sum_jv_j=\sum_{(i,j)\in M}w_{ij}.\]
assumptions_latex: The communication graph is bipartite.
At most one scheduled edge may meet each vertex.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual certificate for node-exclusive maximum-weight scheduling.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent and Bounded-Gap Schedule Fairness
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A required resource may merely recur infinitely often or, more strongly, recur in every window of a fixed length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a schedule \((S_k)\) and required resource \(a\in\mathcal A\), persistent fairness requires \(\lvert\{k:a\in S_k\}\rvert=\infty\). Bounded-gap fairness requires some \(B_a<\infty\) such that \[a\in\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B_a-1}S_t\quad\text{for every }k\ge0.\] Bounded-gap fairness implies persistent fairness, but persistent fairness does not imply a uniform activation-gap bound.
assumptions_latex: The schedule is infinite.
The condition is imposed only on resources declared required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{bounded-gap fairness}\Longrightarrow\text{persistent fairness}\), while the converse need not hold.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two fairness levels for resources required to remain active over an infinite schedule.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling-Subproblem Complexity Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching-based scheduling is polynomially computable, whereas scheduling under an arbitrary conflict graph is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maximum-weight matching is polynomial-time solvable. If feasible simultaneous activations are the independent sets of an arbitrary conflict graph, maximum-weight scheduling is maximum-weight independent set and is NP-hard.
assumptions_latex: Weights are rationally encoded.
Complexity is measured in the explicit graph input size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{maximum-weight matching}\in\mathbf P\), whereas arbitrary conflict-graph maximum-weight scheduling is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tractable matching schedules versus general conflict-graph scheduling.

knowledge_statements.title: Infinite Recurrence Does Not Imply Bounded-Window Connectivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An edge can recur forever while increasingly long silent intervals prevent bounded-window connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On two nodes with sole edge \(e=\{1,2\}\), let \(E_k=\{e\}\) when \(k=2^r\) for some \(r\in\mathbb N\), and let \(E_k=\varnothing\) otherwise. The edge is activated infinitely often, but its activation gaps are unbounded. Consequently, no finite \(B\) makes every \(B\)-round union graph connected.
assumptions_latex: Communication rounds are indexed by nonnegative integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e\text{ activated infinitely often}\not\Longrightarrow\exists B<\infty\text{ such that every }B\text{-round union is connected}.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary separating eventual recurrence from uniform temporal connectivity.

notation.meaning: active edge set at round k

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Activation-Schedule Representation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each round, a communication schedule selects a feasible set of links, nodes, or other communication resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) be a finite set of schedulable communication resources and let \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal F_k\subseteq2^{\mathcal A}\) be the family of simultaneously feasible activations at round \(k\). A communication schedule is a sequence \((S_k)_{k\ge0}\) satisfying \(S_k\in\mathcal F_k\). Link scheduling uses \(\mathcal A=E\), node scheduling uses \(\mathcal A=V\), and a silent round is represented by \(S_k=\varnothing\) when \(\varnothing\in\mathcal F_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is finite.
\(\mathcal F_k\) is nonempty and specified for every round.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified representation of link, node, and communication-resource scheduling constraints.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a communication graph. At slot \(k\), binary variables \(u_i^k\) and \(a_e^k\) indicate active nodes and links, and \(c_k\in\{0,1\}\) indicates whether a communication round occurs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time temporal allocation of communication opportunities, including deterministic, adaptive, or randomized schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A communication schedule is a sequence \(\sigma=((u^k,a^k,c_k))_{k\ge0}\) belonging to a feasibility set \(\Sigma\) that encodes link interference, node availability, bandwidth, and communication-budget restrictions. It is optimization-admissible for a specified method when every information dependency required by that method is activated with the declared recurrence and connectivity property; a standard bounded-window condition is that there exists \(B<\infty\) such that \(\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B-1}\{e\in E:a_e^t=1\}\) is connected for every \(k\), together with \(\sum_{t=0}^{K-1}c_t\le C_K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A communication schedule is the time-indexed allocation of active nodes, links, and communication rounds. It must obey physical and budget constraints and must provide the recurrence or windowed connectivity required by the optimization method. Under a bounded-window model, the union of links used in every consecutive window of fixed length is connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma\in\Sigma\), and bounded-window admissibility requires \(\exists B<\infty\;\forall k:\ (V,\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+B-1}E_t)\text{ is connected}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A randomized schedule may replace deterministic recurrence by positive activation probabilities and an almost-sure connectivity condition.
special_cases_latex: Periodic all-reduce with period \(H\) has \(c_k=1\) exactly when \(k\equiv0\pmod H\).
Full synchronous communication has \(c_k=1\) and \(E_k=E\) for every \(k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The optimization iteration and the communication clock need not have the same index.
boundary_notes: A feasible radio or network schedule need not be optimization-admissible.
Windowed connectivity is one admissibility regime; it is not required by every asynchronous method.
review_flags: The combined scheduling, budget, and window-connectivity definition lacks an inspected exact source locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Priority-based selection from an explicitly declared feasible activation family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given nonnegative round-\(k\) priorities \(w_a^k\) for \(a\in\mathcal A\), choose \[S_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{S\in\mathcal F_k}\sum_{a\in S}w_a^k.\] Ties are resolved by a declared deterministic or randomized rule. The policy is exact only when the displayed maximization is solved exactly; an \(\alpha\)-approximate scheduler instead returns \(S_k\) whose score is at least \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) times the maximum score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activate the feasible resource set of largest current priority, or a declared approximation to it.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F_k\) is nonempty.
The priorities are available before the round-k decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{a\in S_k}w_a^k=\max_{S\in\mathcal F_k}\sum_{a\in S}w_a^k\) for exact scheduling.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infinite Recurrence Does Not Give Bounded-Window Connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp distinction between eventual recurrence and uniform temporal connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the two-node graph with sole edge \(e=\{1,2\}\), set \(E_k=\{e\}\) when \(k=2^r\) for some \(r\in\mathbb N\), and \(E_k=\varnothing\) otherwise. The edge is activated infinitely often, but its activation gaps \(2^{r+1}-2^r=2^r\) are unbounded. Hence no finite \(B\) makes every \(B\)-round union graph connected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An edge can recur forever while increasingly long silent intervals prevent bounded-window connectivity.
assumptions_latex: Communication rounds are indexed by nonnegative integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e\text{ is activated infinitely often}\not\Rightarrow\exists B<\infty\text{ such that every }B\text{-window is connected}.\)

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At round \(k\), worker \(i\) has workload \(\ell_i^k\), completion time \(T_i^k\), returned update \(g_i^k\), and inclusion weight \(w_i^k\). Let \(A_k\) be the set of responses accepted before a stopping rule or deadline.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributed methods that adapt workload assignment, response selection, aggregation weights, or redundancy to heterogeneous and time-varying completion times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed method is straggler-load adaptive if its control \((\ell^k,A_k,w^k)\) is measurable with respect to information available by round \(k\), satisfies the resource constraints, and forms an aggregate \(g^k=\sum_{i\in A_k}w_i^kg_i^k\) whose declared target is preserved. In an unbiased stochastic formulation this requires \(\mathbb E[g^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla F(x^k)\); in a deterministic coded formulation it requires exact recoverability of the prescribed aggregate from every response set in a declared family \(\mathcal A_k\). The family is adaptive when at least one control changes with observed load or latency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A method in this family changes workload, accepted responders, aggregation weights, or redundancy using observed system state. The resulting aggregate must retain a declared mathematical validity condition, such as conditional unbiasedness or exact coded recovery, while satisfying resource limits. Merely dropping slow workers without correcting the induced objective weighting does not meet this definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g^k=\sum_{i\in A_k}w_i^kg_i^k\) is resource-feasible and either \(\mathbb E[g^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla F(x^k)\) or is exactly recoverable for all \(A_k\in\mathcal A_k\).
special_cases_latex: A fixed deadline policy takes \(A_k=\{i:T_i^k\le d_k\}\).
Gradient coding is the exact-recovery special case with redundant assigned workloads.
immediate_consequences_latex: Response-time adaptation must be analyzed together with the statistical or algebraic validity of the aggregate.
boundary_notes: Conditional unbiasedness and exact coded recovery are alternative regimes, not simultaneous requirements.
The definition does not guarantee reduced wall-clock time or convergence.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permanently ignoring a worker can make an asynchronous method optimize the wrong objective.

Worker 2 is permanently starved.

knowledge_statements.title: Straggler-Aware Optimization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update immediately when a worker responds, weighting its delayed gradient by the objective weight divided by its selection probability, without waiting at a global barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i f_i(x)\), initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb R^d\) and a server counter \(k=0\). Stop after a prescribed number of accepted gradients or when a stated stationarity test is met, and output the latest iterate.

The objective weights satisfy \(p_i\geq0\) and \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1\).

Returned gradients have delay at most \(\tau_{\max}<\infty\).

Greedy Load-Aware List Scheduling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-loaded assignment has a standard constant-factor guarantee, improved by assigning longer jobs first.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For jobs with processing times \(p_j>0\) on \(m\) identical workers, list scheduling assigns each successive job to a currently least-loaded worker. Its makespan satisfies \[T_{\rm LS}\le\left(2-\frac1m\right)T^\star.\] The longest-processing-time-first variant orders jobs by nonincreasing \(p_j\) and, for \(m\ge2\), satisfies \[T_{\rm LPT}\le\left(\frac43-\frac1{3m}\right)T^\star.\]
assumptions_latex: Jobs are independent and indivisible.
Workers are identical and processing times are known.
Migration and communication costs are excluded.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initial assignment of indivisible tasks using predicted worker loads.

notation.meaning: predicted processing time of job j

knowledge_statements.title: Indivisible Load Assignment Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal indivisible load balancing is NP-hard although continuously divisible constant-rate allocation has a closed form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Minimizing \(\max_i\sum_{j\in A_i}p_j\) over partitions of indivisible jobs among at least two identical workers is NP-hard; for two workers its decision form contains PARTITION. Thus continuous equal-finish allocation does not extend exactly to indivisible jobs.
assumptions_latex: Job sizes are positive integers encoded in binary.
Every job is assigned wholly to one worker.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial boundary absent from continuously divisible allocation.

knowledge_statements.title: Rate-Misestimation Makespan Boundary
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proportional allocation can perform arbitrarily badly when a worker's service rate is severely overestimated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(b_i=B\hat s_i/\sum_j\hat s_j\) is assigned using predicted rates but actual rates are \(s_i>0\), then \[T=\frac{B}{\sum_j\hat s_j}\max_i\frac{\hat s_i}{s_i},\qquad \frac{T}{T^\star}=\frac{\sum_i s_i}{\sum_j\hat s_j}\max_i\frac{\hat s_i}{s_i}.\] A sufficiently severe rate overestimate can therefore make the realized makespan arbitrarily worse than the actual-rate optimum.
assumptions_latex: Work is divisible.
Predicted and actual rates are positive and constant during the batch.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robustness limit of allocation based on predicted service rates.

notation.meaning: predicted service rate of worker i

knowledge_statements.title: Load-Aware Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static divisible-work allocation minimizing predicted parallel makespan.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given total divisible work \(M>0\) and positive worker rates \(r_i\), solve \(\min_{a_i\ge0}\max_i a_i/r_i\) subject to \(\sum_i a_i=M\). Assign \(a_i^*=Mr_i/(\sum_jr_j)\) units to worker \(i\), execute the corresponding local oracle calls, aggregate their correctly scaled contributions, and update the optimization iterate. Re-estimate rates after an epoch and repeat the allocation if the rate model changes. The allocation equalizes predicted completion times: \(a_i^*/r_i=M/(\sum_jr_j)\) for every worker. Stop according to the enclosing optimization method and return its terminal iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate divisible work in proportion to measured worker rates, equalizing predicted completion times while preserving the optimization aggregate.
assumptions_latex: The workload is divisible and worker \(i\) processes it at constant rate \(r_i>0\) during an epoch.
Redistributing work does not change the aggregate oracle quantity after scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^*\) minimizes the predicted epoch makespan, whose value is \(M/(\sum_jr_j)\).

notation.meaning: predicted processing rate of worker i

knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Work-Stealing Redistribution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Idle workers steal atomically owned unstarted work while preserving exactly-once execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an atomic owner for every unstarted unit and a deque at each worker. An idle worker atomically transfers a declared batch from a donor's unstarted tail. Completed or executing units are not stolen. Terminate only when all deques are empty, no unit is executing, and no transfer is in flight.
assumptions_latex: Ownership transfer is atomic.
Only unstarted work is transferable.
Termination detection accounts for queued, executing, and in-flight work.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every initial work unit is executed exactly once, and detected termination implies no work remains.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic conservative migration of unstarted work units.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Redistribution Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching primal and dual objectives, equivalently full complementary slackness, certifies optimal redistribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Primal and dual feasible points certify optimality when \(T=\sum_j\lambda_jd_j-vH\). Equivalently, complementary slackness requires \(u_i(\sum_j a_{ij}/s_i-T)=0\), \(v(\sum_{i,j}h_{ij}a_{ij}-H)=0\), \(a_{ij}(u_i/s_i+vh_{ij}-\lambda_j)=0\), and \(T(1-\sum_i u_i)=0\).
assumptions_latex: The candidates are feasible for the displayed primal and dual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate for the divisible-load linear program.
review_flags: Corrected the builder certificate by adding complementary slackness for the nonnegative makespan variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Migration Break-Even Condition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Migration is worthwhile exactly when saved execution time exceeds critical-path migration overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(T_0\) is completion time without migration, \(T_1\) is post-redistribution execution makespan excluding migration, and \(C_{\rm mig}\) is critical-path migration time, redistribution helps exactly when \(C_{\rm mig}+T_1<T_0\).
assumptions_latex: All terms use one consistent nonoverlap timing model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock condition for beneficial redistribution under a declared timing model.
review_flags: Overlap or contention requires the corresponding critical-path replacement.

knowledge_statements.title: Conservative Workload Redistribution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redistribution moves execution responsibility while conserving every original workload.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_j\ge0\) be work initially owned by participant \(j\), and let \(a_{ij}\ge0\) be the amount ultimately executed by \(i\) for \(j\). Redistribution is conservative when \[\sum_i a_{ij}=d_j\quad\text{for every }j,\] and is nontrivial when some \(a_{ij}>0\) with \(i\ne j\).
assumptions_latex: Work is divisible and exactly recombinable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservation law distinguishing migration from dropping or replicating work.

notation.meaning: work executed by i on behalf of original owner j

knowledge_statements.title: Dual of Divisible Makespan Redistribution
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The redistribution dual prices original loads, executor time, and the transfer budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{a\ge0,T\ge0}T\) subject to \(\sum_i a_{ij}=d_j\), \(\sum_j a_{ij}/s_i\le T\), and \(\sum_{i,j}h_{ij}a_{ij}\le H\), the dual is \(\max_{\lambda,u,v}\sum_j\lambda_jd_j-vH\) subject to \(u_i,v\ge0\), \(\sum_i u_i\le1\), and \(\lambda_j\le u_i/s_i+vh_{ij}\) for all \(i,j\), with \(\lambda_j\) free.
assumptions_latex: Loads are divisible.
The primal is feasible and finite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual pricing of load conservation, executor capacity, and transfer budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Indivisible Redistribution Is Combinatorial
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal redistribution becomes NP-hard when jobs cannot be split, even with zero transfer costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If each job must be transferred and executed as an indivisible unit, makespan-minimizing redistribution contains identical-machine scheduling as its zero-transfer-cost special case and is NP-hard. A divisible redistribution linear program therefore need not solve the indivisible problem.
assumptions_latex: Jobs have integer sizes and remain indivisible.
Transfer costs may be zero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of divisible linear redistribution models.

knowledge_statements.title: Workload Redistribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epochwise migration of unfinished divisible work from overloaded workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At redistribution time \(t\), let \(u_i^t\ge0\) be worker \(i\)'s unfinished work and \(r_i^t>0\) its estimated rate. Choose transfers \(z_{ij}^t\ge0\) by minimizing \(\max_i (u_i^t-\sum_jz_{ij}^t+\sum_jz_{ji}^t)/r_i^t\), subject to \(\sum_jz_{ij}^t\le u_i^t\) and any migration-capacity constraints. Replace each workload by \(u_i^{t+}=u_i^t-\sum_jz_{ij}^t+\sum_jz_{ji}^t\), preserving \(\sum_i u_i^{t+}=\sum_i u_i^t\). Migrate the associated data or oracle indices, continue computation, and output the enclosing method's terminal iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Periodically transfer unfinished work to minimize predicted makespan, subject to migration limits, while conserving total work and oracle contributions.
assumptions_latex: Unfinished tasks are divisible or transferable without duplication.
Rate estimates remain valid over the next redistribution epoch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The redistribution conserves total unfinished work and minimizes the modeled post-transfer makespan over the feasible transfer set.

notation.meaning: work transferred from worker i to worker j

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any fully specified linear redistribution model, a primal feasible assignment \((a,T)\) and dual feasible multipliers certify optimality when their objective values agree. In particular, equality of the achieved makespan and a dual lower bound is necessary and sufficient for optimality by linear-programming strong duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible redistribution is globally optimal when a feasible dual prices load conservation, worker capacity, and transfer budget at the same objective value.
assumptions_latex: The redistribution model is a feasible finite-dimensional linear program with finite optimum.
review_flags: The exact dual equations depend on the declared transfer-cost and capacity model.

Quorum Response Mitigation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quorum limits waiting to the q-th response, while inclusion-probability correction can preserve the target aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dispatch a common iterate to \(n\) workers and update after the first \(q\) admissible responses, \(1\le q\le n\), so round latency is \(T_{(q)}\). If the accepted subset \(S\) has known inclusion probabilities \(\pi_i>0\), then the Horvitz--Thompson aggregate \(\sum_{i\in S}(p_i/\pi_i)g_i\) is unbiased for \(\sum_i p_ig_i\), provided the inclusion model correctly accounts for response selection.
assumptions_latex: Exactly the first \(q\) admissible responses are accepted.
The inclusion probabilities are positive and correctly specified.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Waiting for the first q admissible responses rather than every assigned worker.
review_flags: Correction is invalid if the stated inclusion model omits dependence between response times and returned values.

knowledge_statements.title: MDS-Coded Exact Linear Recovery
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An MDS-coded linear response model recovers the exact aggregate from any m of n responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\), let \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) have every \(m\)-row submatrix nonsingular, and let worker \(i\) return \(y_i=\sum_{s=1}^mC_{is}g_s\). From any responding set \(S\) of size \(m\), \(C_S\) is invertible, so all \(g_s\), and hence \(\sum_sg_s\), are recovered exactly. The recovery threshold is \(m\).
assumptions_latex: Shard contributions combine linearly.
Workers can form the coded responses exactly.
Every \(m\)-row submatrix of \(C\) is nonsingular.

knowledge_statements.title: Latency–Redundant-Work Accounting for Replication
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replication improves the minimum completion-time distribution but can multiply launched work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r\) independent identically distributed nonnegative replica times with CDF \(F\), \(\mathbb E[T_{(1)}]=\int_0^\infty(1-F(t))^r\,dt\). Launching \(r\) copies uses at most \(r\) times the unreplicated work before cancellation.
assumptions_latex: Replica times are independent and identically distributed for the latency formula.
The work bound conservatively counts all launched copies.

knowledge_statements.title: Correlated Replicas Need Not Reduce Tail Latency
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replication cannot remove common-mode stalls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If all replica completion times satisfy \(T_j=T\) almost surely, then \(\min_{j\le r}T_j=T\) for every \(r\). Perfect common-mode dependence therefore yields no latency reduction while potentially multiplying executed work by \(r\).
assumptions_latex: Replica completion times are perfectly dependent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{(1)}=T\) almost surely for every replica count \(r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence boundary for speculative-execution benefits.

knowledge_statements.title: Replica Completion as an Order Statistic
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent replication replaces shard latency by a minimum order statistic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r\) independent replica times with common distribution function \(F\), \[\Pr(\min_{j\le r}T_j>t)=(1-F(t))^r.\] If the times are exponential with rate \(\mu\), the minimum is exponential with rate \(r\mu\) and mean \(1/(r\mu)\).
assumptions_latex: Replica times are independent and identically distributed.
The mean specialization assumes exponential times of rate \(\mu\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Latency law for speculative replication under an explicit stochastic model.

knowledge_statements.title: Tail-Latency Mitigation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundant task dispatch with first-completion acceptance and cancellation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition an iteration into \(m\) logical tasks. For task \(j\), dispatch \(r_j\ge1\) equivalent replicas to distinct workers and accept the first valid result arriving before deadline \(\tau_j\); cancel or discard later replicas. Let replica completion times be \(C_{j,1},\ldots,C_{j,r_j}\). The logical completion time is \(L_j=\min_{1\le k\le r_j}C_{j,k}\), and the iteration completes at \(L=\max_{1\le j\le m}L_j\). Aggregate exactly one result per logical task, perform the enclosing optimization update, and stop by its prescribed rule. Replication factors must satisfy the available compute budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replicate logical tasks, accept each task's first valid completion, discard duplicates, and aggregate exactly once to reduce iteration tail latency.
assumptions_latex: Replicas of a logical task return equivalent deterministic results or identically distributed unbiased results.
Duplicate results are identifiable and cannot be counted twice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every realization, \(L_j\le C_{j,k}\) for each replica \(k\), while single-count aggregation preserves the intended logical workload.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete compute–communication–precision design can be Pareto efficient yet unsupported by every linear resource weighting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider three accuracy-feasible designs with two minimized resource costs \(r(d_1)=(0,2)\), \(r(d_2)=(1,1.1)\), and \(r(d_3)=(2,0)\). knowledge_statements.title: Pareto Compute–Communication–Precision Co-Design
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A joint design is Pareto efficient when no equally accurate design uses no more of every declared resource and strictly less of at least one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\in\mathcal D\) jointly specify local computation, communication frequency or volume, and message precision. Let \(Q(d)\) be a common quality measure and \(r(d)=(r_{\rm comp}(d),r_{\rm comm}(d),r_{\rm bits}(d),r_{\rm time}(d))\) be consistently accounted resource costs. For target \(\varepsilon\), a feasible design \(d^\star\) with \(Q(d^\star)\le\varepsilon\) is Pareto efficient if no feasible \(d\) satisfies \(r_j(d)\le r_j(d^\star)\) for every component with strict inequality in at least one component.
assumptions_latex: All compared designs use the same quality criterion and target \(\varepsilon\).
Resource components use consistent accounting conventions.
Each design specifies computation, communication, and precision choices.

knowledge_statements.title: No Universal Three-Resource Tradeoff Law

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Pareto dominance alone imposes no universal numerical relation among computation, communication, and precision. Any finite mutually nondominating set of resource vectors can be the feasible resource image of an abstract design problem.
assumptions_latex: Only feasibility and componentwise resource minimization are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A numerical three-way rate or controller requires a method-specific error and timing model.}
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on conclusions available without an optimizer, compressor, and timing model.

knowledge_statements.title: Budgeted Scalarization of Joint Resource Design
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted resource minimization yields weakly Pareto-efficient designs, and positive weights yield Pareto-efficient designs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_\varepsilon=\{d\in\mathcal D:Q(d)\le\varepsilon\}\) and let \(r(d)\in\mathbb R_+^m\) contain consistently measured resource costs. For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\), solve \(\min_{d\in\mathcal F_\varepsilon}\lambda^{\mathsf T}r(d)\). Every minimizer is weakly Pareto efficient; if \(\lambda_j>0\) for every \(j\), every minimizer is Pareto efficient.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F_\varepsilon\ne\varnothing\) and the minimum is attained.
All resource coordinates are minimized and consistently accounted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d^\star\in\arg\min_{d\in\mathcal F_\varepsilon}\lambda^{\mathsf T}r(d)\Rightarrow d^\star\text{ is weakly Pareto efficient; if }\lambda>0\text{, it is Pareto efficient}.

knowledge_statements.title: Compute–Communication–Precision Co-Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained resource model coupling local steps, rounds, and message bits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb N\) be local oracle calls per communication round, \(R\in\mathbb N\) the number of rounds, and \(b\in\mathbb N\) the transmitted bits per coordinate. Given a validated error upper bound \(\mathcal E(R,H,b)\), per-call cost \(c_{\rm comp}>0\), and communication cost \(c_{\rm comm}(b)>0\), the co-design problem is \[\min_{R,H,b} R\bigl(Hc_{\rm comp}+c_{\rm comm}(b)\bigr)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \mathcal E(R,H,b)\le\varepsilon.\] Any minimizer \((R^*,H^*,b^*)\) jointly specifies local computation, exchange frequency, and message precision. The chosen distributed method is then run for \(R^*\) rounds with \(H^*\) local calls and \(b^*\)-bit messages.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose local work, communication rounds, and message precision jointly to minimize modeled cost while meeting a validated error target.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal E\) is a valid error bound for the selected distributed algorithm and quantizer.
All costs use a common time, energy, or monetary unit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((R^*,H^*,b^*)\) is feasible for accuracy \(\varepsilon\) and minimizes the stated modeled resource cost.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed right-preconditioned GMRES applies the KKT operator and preconditioner in parallel, uses global reductions for Arnoldi orthogonalization, returns immediately when the initial or a later iterate meets the residual tolerance, and explicitly reports nonconvergent Arnoldi breakdown or exhaustion of the iteration limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Kx=b\) be a distributed nonsingular KKT system, let \(M^{-1}\) be a fixed applicable right preconditioner, let \(0<\varepsilon<1\), and let \(j_{\max}\ge 1\) be an iteration limit. Choose \(x_0\), set \(r_0=b-Kx_0\), and set \(\beta=\lVert r_0\rVert_2\). If \(\beta\le\varepsilon\lVert b\rVert_2\), return \(x_0\). Otherwise set \(v_1=r_0/\beta\). At Arnoldi step \(j\), processes compute \(z_j=M^{-1}v_j\) and the distributed product \(w=Kz_j\); for \(i=1,\ldots,j\), they obtain \(h_{ij}=v_i^{\mathsf T}w\) by global reduction and update \(w\leftarrow w-h_{ij}v_i\). Set \(h_{j+1,j}=\lVert w\rVert_2\), form the Arnoldi matrix \(\overline H_j\), compute \(y_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_y\lVert\beta e_1-\overline H_jy\rVert_2\), and set \(x_j=x_0+Z_jy_j\), where \(Z_j=[z_1,\ldots,z_j]\). If \(\lVert b-Kx_j\rVert_2\le\varepsilon\lVert b\rVert_2\), return \(x_j\). If \(h_{j+1,j}=0\) and the residual test fails, report Arnoldi breakdown; otherwise set \(v_{j+1}=w/h_{j+1,j}\) and continue. Report failure if no iterate passes the residual test by step \(j_{\max}\).
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular, \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}\), and the distributed product by \(K\) is available.
\(M\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) is fixed and nonsingular, and each application of \(M^{-1}\) is well defined.
\(0<\varepsilon<1\) and \(j_{\max}\in\mathbb{N}\) with \(j_{\max}\ge1\).
Exact residuals are evaluated at the declared stopping points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On successful termination, the returned iterate \(x\) satisfies \(\lVert b-Kx\rVert_2\le\varepsilon\lVert b\rVert_2\); otherwise the algorithm reports Arnoldi breakdown or exhaustion of \(j_{\max}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Communication-avoiding Krylov solve
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method groups several Krylov products before a batched orthogonalization, reducing synchronization while retaining a block minimal-residual update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Ax=b\), an initial vector \(x_0\), block length \(s\ge2\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\), set \(r_0=b-Ax_0\). At outer iteration \(j\), generate the local polynomial block \(W_j=[r_j,Ar_j,\ldots,A^{s-1}r_j]\) using \(s-1\) successive distributed matrix-vector products without intervening inner-product reductions. Use one batched collective orthogonalization, such as block Gram computation followed by TSQR, to obtain a basis \(Q_j\) for \(\mathcal{K}_s(A,r_j)\). Compute \(z_j\in\operatorname*{argmin}_z\lVert r_j-AQ_jz\rVert_2\), set \(x_{j+1}=x_j+Q_jz_j\), and recompute \(r_{j+1}\). Stop when \(\lVert r_{j+1}\rVert_2\le\varepsilon\lVert b\rVert_2\), or report the iteration limit.

Distributed products by \(A\) and stable batched orthogonalization are available.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Benders subproblem solve
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers solve independent scenario recourse problems, return Benders optimality or feasibility cuts, and the coordinator adds all cuts before resolving the master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a master iterate \(x^k\), dispatch every scenario \(s\in S\) to a worker. The worker solves \[Q_s(x^k)=\min_{y_s\ge 0}\{q_s^{\mathsf T}y_s:W_sy_s=h_s-T_sx^k\}.\] If the problem is feasible and bounded, it returns an optimal dual vector \(\pi_s^k\) and the cut \(\theta_s\ge (\pi_s^k)^{\mathsf T}(h_s-T_sx)\), where \(W_s^{\mathsf T}\pi_s^k\le q_s\). If it is infeasible, it returns a dual ray \(r_s^k\) satisfying \(W_s^{\mathsf T}r_s^k\le0\) and the feasibility cut \((r_s^k)^{\mathsf T}(h_s-T_sx)\le0\). After all workers finish, add every returned cut, resolve the master, and stop when no violated feasibility cut remains and every recourse gap is within tolerance.

The current master solution \(x^k\) is available identically to all workers.
Each worker returns either a valid optimal dual solution or a valid infeasibility ray.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous decomposition worker
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers evaluate decomposition oracles on possibly stale tagged states; the coordinator incorporates admissible messages immediately and rejects updates exceeding a fixed delay bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a coordinator maintain states \(v^0,v^1,\ldots\) and let worker \(i\) implement a decomposition oracle \(\mathcal O_i\). Worker \(i\) reads a tagged state \((v^{\tau},\tau)\), computes \(m_i=\mathcal O_i(v^{\tau})\), and returns \((i,m_i,\tau)\) without waiting for other workers. Upon the \(k\)-th accepted arrival, the coordinator accepts the message only if \(0\le k-\tau\le D\), then performs \[v^{k+1}=\mathcal U(v^k;i,m_i,\tau).\] A message with \(k-\tau>D\) is discarded or assigned a fresh state. Every worker message identifies its worker and the state version used to compute it.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block workers independently minimize reduced cost under common master dual prices; all improving columns are added together before the restricted master is resolved.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver task queue
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Source tasks initially enter a precedence-aware FIFO queue. An idle worker atomically moves the first queued task into the running set. Successful completion releases previously unqueued successors whose predecessors are complete, while failure returns the task to the queue. The procedure stops exactly when every task is complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite directed acyclic task graph, where \((u,v)\in E\) means that task \(v\) requires the output of task \(u\). Let \(Q\) be an ordered queue, \(R\subseteq V\) the set of running tasks, and \(C\subseteq V\) the set of successfully completed tasks. Initialize \(R=C=\varnothing\) and initialize \(Q\) with all tasks \(v\in V\) satisfying \(\operatorname{pred}(v)=\varnothing\), ordered by a fixed tie-breaking key. Whenever a worker becomes idle and \(Q\) is nonempty, atomically remove the first task \(u\) from \(Q\), add \(u\) to \(R\), and assign it to that worker. If \(u\) succeeds, atomically remove it from \(R\), add it to \(C\), and enqueue, in tie-breaking order, every task \(v\in V\setminus(C\cup R\cup\operatorname{elts}(Q))\) satisfying \(\operatorname{pred}(v)\subseteq C\). If \(u\) fails, atomically remove it from \(R\) and append it to \(Q\) without adding it to \(C\). Stop and return the task outputs exactly when \(C=V\).
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite directed acyclic graph.
Queue, running-set, and completed-set transitions are atomic.
Every running task eventually reports either success or failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every task moved from \(Q\) to \(R\) has all predecessors in \(C\), no task occupies two execution states simultaneously, and the procedure stops exactly when \(C=V\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A precedence-aware FIFO queue for dispatching finite solver tasks to distributed workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Barrier synchronization in parallel solves
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A barrier prevents every worker from passing into the next superstep until all participants have arrived. Its release time is no earlier than the last arrival, and each early worker waits until release; in an ideal zero-overhead model, release occurs at the last-arrival time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(p\geq1\) workers executing supersteps \(k=0,1,\ldots\). Let \(a_i^k\) be the time at which worker \(i\) reaches the barrier ending superstep \(k\), and define the last-arrival time by \[b^k=\max_{1\leq j\leq p}a_j^k.\] A barrier synchronization prevents every worker from passing the barrier and beginning superstep \(k+1\) before all participating workers have arrived. If \(r^k\) is the logical release time, then \(r^k\geq b^k\). Writing \(\lambda^k=r^k-b^k\geq0\) for barrier-release latency, worker \(i\) waits \(w_i^k=r^k-a_i^k\). In the ideal zero-overhead barrier model, \(\lambda^k=0\) and hence \(r^k=b^k\).
assumptions_latex: The participant set \(\{1,ldots,p\}\) is fixed during each barrier instance.
Every participating worker eventually reaches the barrier.
Barrier arrivals and the logical release event are reliably recorded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every worker \(i\), passage into superstep \(k+1\) occurs no earlier than \(r^k\geq b^k=\max_j a_j^k\), and its barrier waiting time is \(w_i^k=r^k-a_i^k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous solver communication
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers send versioned states without blocking, retain each neighbor's newest received state, and update from local caches without waiting at a global barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Worker \(i\) stores local state \(x_i\), local version \(v_i\), and the newest received pair \((v_j,x_j)\) for each required neighbor \(j\). After any local update, it increments \(v_i\) and sends \((i,v_i,x_i)\) without waiting for acknowledgments or other workers. Upon receiving \((j,v,x)\), it replaces the cached pair for \(j\) exactly when \(v\) exceeds the cached version. Whenever locally activated, worker \(i\) computes its next solver update from its current state and cached neighbor states. Execution uses no global barrier and stops only when a distributed termination certificate is obtained; otherwise it produces an asynchronous state sequence indefinitely.
